notesEn: Exercise 1: Add the word (هٰذَا) to the following words and read them: كُرْسِيٌّ ، عَمُوْدٌ ، سَقْفٌ ، كَأْسٌ ، وَرَقٌ ، تِلْمِيْذٌ ، خَادِمٌ ، مُعَلِّمٌ ، يُوْسُفُ ، حَارِسٌ — e.g. هٰذَا كُرْسِيٌّ … etc.
Some grammatical definitions: Ism Ishaara (إِسْمُ الْإِشَارَة) is a word that points towards something, e.g. هٰذَا كِتَابٌ.
Masculine: e.g. رَجُلٌ ، فَرَسٌ ، حَجَرٌ ، مَاءٌ.
The Rule: The word هٰذَا is an Ism Ishaara and is used for single masculine words that are close by, e.g. هٰذَا كِتَابٌ means "this is a book" (not "that is a book").
مَا؟ - This word is used to ask about something.
مَنْ؟ - This word is used to ask about someone.

The Rule: The word هٰذِهِ is an Ism Ishaara and used for single feminine words that are close by. Feminine words are usually recognised by the letter (ة), which appears at the end of the word and, when stopping, is read as the letter (ه).

Exercise 3: Convert the following sentences to the feminine gender: هٰذَا صَالِحٌ، هٰذَا كَاتِبٌ، هٰذَا مُتَعَلِّمٌ، أَنْتَ وَلَدٌ، هٰذَا شَرِيْفٌ، هُوَ كَرِيْمٌ، هُوَ مَرِيْضٌ، أَنَا تِلْمِيْذٌ، أَنْتَ أُسْتَاذٌ، هُوَ وَلَدٌ.
Some grammatical definitions: اسم الضمير (Ismud-Dameer) - a noun that denotes the first, second or third person in a sentence, e.g. هُوَ ، أَنْتَ ، أَنَا etc.
المتكلم - The speaker, i.e. the first person.
المخاطب - The person being addressed, i.e. the second person.
الغائب - The person who is being spoken about, i.e. the third person.

Exercise 1: Add the letter (ي) to the following words and then read them, e.g. هٰذَا رَأْسِيْ — هٰذَا رَأْسٌ، هٰذَا وَجْهٌ، هٰذَا أَنْفٌ، هٰذَا فَمٌ، هٰذَا قَلْبٌ، هٰذَا لِسَانٌ، هٰذَا صَدْرٌ، هٰذَا بَطْنٌ، هٰذَا ظَهْرٌ، هٰذَا جِلْدٌ.
Exercise 2: Add the letter (كَ) to the same list of words and then read them, e.g. هٰذَا رَأْسُكَ.
The Rule: Whenever the speaker wishes to attribute anything to himself, he adds the letter (ي) to the end of the word, regardless of whether he is male or female, e.g. قَلَمِيْ ، كِتَابِيْ.
The Rule: When attributing something to a male who is being addressed, add the letter (كَ) (with a Fatha) to the end of the word.
The Rule: When attributing something to a female who is being addressed, add the letter (كِ) (with a Kasra) to the end of the word.
Each of these letters added to the word is called a ضمير.
When asking about whom something belongs to use the word لِمَنْ.

notesEn: This lesson is a dictation lesson (أَلْإِمْلَاءُ): the words and sentences below are meant to be dictated, not translated.

Dictation word list (أَلْمُفْرَدَاتُ): هٰذَا ، ذَاكَ ، ذٰلِكَ ، هٰذِهِ ، تِلْكَ ، قَلَمٌ ، شُبَّاكٌ ، عَمُوْدٌ ، سَقْفٌ ، سَطْحٌ ، حَارِسٌ ، زَهْرَةٌ ، مِسْطَرَةٌ ، مِحْفَظَةٌ ، مُوَظَّفَةٌ ، مَسْرُوْرَةٌ.

Note (مَلْحُوْظَة): The respected teacher should dictate this lesson to the students, then go through their exercise books and correct the mistakes, then explain the rules of dictation to them and instruct them to write the passage out again correctly — and the same is to be done in the dictation lessons that follow.
Some Principles of Dictation 1: The masculine اسم اشارة word هٰذَا is written without the letter ا, although it is pronounced as هاذا.
Some Principles of Dictation 2: The feminine اسم اشارة word هٰذِهِ is written without the letter ا, although it is pronounced as هاذه.

notesEn: Exercise 1 (not a translation drill): convert the following words into dual nouns, e.g. رَأْسٌ becomes رَأْسَانِ — رَأْسٌ، لِسَانٌ، قَلْبٌ، صَدْرٌ، بَطْنٌ، عَيْنٌ، شَفَةٌ، سَاقٌ، قَدَمٌ، رِجْلٌ.

Exercise 2 (not a translation drill): use the following dual words in sentences. Masculine: وَجْهَانِ، أَنْفَانِ، فَمَانِ، بَطْنَانِ، ظَهْرَانِ، جِسْمَانِ، حَجَرَانِ، جِدَارَانِ. Feminine: يَدَانِ، أُذُنَانِ، كَتِفَانِ، فَخِذَانِ، رُكْبَتَانِ، سَيَّارَتَانِ، زَهْرَتَانِ، شَجَرَتَانِ. The book's examples are هٰذَانِ، وَجْهَانِ، هَاتَانِ، يَدَانِ.
The Rule: the Dhameer نَحْنُ is used for the speaker and applies equally to singular, dual and plural.
The Rule: the Dhameer أَنْتُمَا is used for the second person in the dual form and applies equally to both masculine and feminine.
The Rule: the Dhameer هُمَا is used for the third person in the dual form and applies equally to both masculine and feminine.
When referring to two different things, they will be stated individually with the conjunction وَ between them, e.g. هٰذَانِ خَالِدٌ وَمَحْمُوْدٌ، هَاتَانِ فَاطِمَةُ وَزَيْنَبُ.

N.B. Parts of the body that are singular are usually masculine (e.g. رَأْسٌ، أَنْفٌ), while those that are paired are usually feminine (e.g. عَيْنٌ) even though they may not have the letter (ة) at the end.

notesEn: The Rule: a verb in the present or future tense is called فِعْلُ مُضَارِعٌ.

The Rule: the plural speaker of the مُضَارِع verb is recognised by the letter ( ن ) at the beginning, e.g. نَذْهَبُ.

notesEn: Some Principles of Dictation — ( و ): although only one ( و ) is written in the word دَاوُدُ, it is read as two, i.e. دَاوُوْدُ. However, in other similar words the letter ( و ) is both written and read, e.g. طَاوُوْسٌ.

Some Principles of Dictation — there are some words in which the ( و ) is written but not read, e.g. written أُولُوْا / read أُلُوْ ; written أُولٰئِكَ / read أُلَآئِكَ ; written أُولِيْ / read أُلِيْ ; written عَمْرُو / read عَمْرُ.

notesEn: The Rule: The singular speaker of the feminine مضارع verb is recognised by the letter (أ) at the beginning, e.g. أَجْلِسُ.

The Rule: The singular second person of the مضارع verb is recognised by the letter (ت) at the beginning and the letters (ين) at the end, e.g. تَجْلِسِيْنَ. (The book prints 'first second person' here.)
The Rule: The singular third person of the مضارع verb is recognised by the letter (ت) at the beginning, e.g. تَجْلِسُ.

The Command: when the second person is told to carry out an act, the command phrase is called فعل أمر. It is made from the مضارع verb by removing the signs by which the مضارع verb is recognised. If the letter after that letter of recognition is Saakin (carries a Sukoon), the word receives a Hamza (ا) at the beginning and the last letter receives a Sukoon, e.g. تَقْرَأُ becomes اِقْرَأْ and تَفْتَحُ becomes اِفْتَحْ.

The Command: if the letter after the letter of recognition is Mutaharrik (carries a Harkat), no Hamza is added at the beginning, though the last letter still receives a Sukoon, e.g. تَقِفُ becomes قِفْ. The command is made feminine by adding the letter ي at the end, e.g. اِفْتَحْ becomes اِفْتَحِيْ.

notesEn: Some Principles of Dictation: the round letter ة (أَلتَّاءُ الْمَرْبُوْطَةُ) is written in its rounded form when it comes at the end of a noun in the singular with a fatha before it, e.g. فَاطِمَةُ، قَاهِرَةُ، طَالِبَةٌ، مُعَلِّمَةٌ. It is written the same way at the end of a broken plural (جَمْع تَكْسِيْر), that is the plural of a word ending in the letter (ي), e.g. غَزَاةٌ the plural of غَازِيْ, قَضَاةٌ the plural of قَاضِي, and دُعَاةٌ the plural of دَاعِيْ.
The Rule: when welcoming a guest, greet with the words أَهْلًا وَسَهْلًا وَمَرْحَبًا.

The Arabic side is headed أَلْإِمْلَاءُ (dictation). Its first section أَلْمُفْرَدَاتُ is a list of words for dictation practice, with no English given: تَأْخُذِيْنَ ، تَفْتَحِيْنَ ، تَقْرَئِيْنَ ، تُغْلِقِيْنَ ، تَقُوْمِيْنَ ، تَمْشِيْنَ ، تَخْرُجِيْنَ ، تَذْهَبِيْنَ ، مَكَّةُ الْمُكَرَّمَةُ ، يَضَعُ ، يُغْلِقُ ، يَكْتُبُ ، صُنْدُوْقُ الْبَرِيْدِ ، أَلظَّرْفُ ، طَابِعٌ ، دَفْتَرُ الْحُضُوْرِ.

His teachers and his classmates love him

notesEn: Some Principles of Dictation. The long letter ت (أَلتَّاءُ الْمَفْتُوحَة) is written: 1. at the end of verbs, regardless of whether the letter before it has a harakat or a sukoon, e.g. فَهِمْتُ، عَلِمْتُ، سَمِعْتُ - فَهِمَتْ، عَلِمَتْ، سَمِعَتْ.
2. at the end of verbs when the letter ت is amongst the root letters of the word, e.g. ثَبَتَ يَثْبُتُ، سَكَتَ يَسْكُتُ، بَاتَ يَبِيتُ، مَاتَ يَمُوتُ.
3. at the end of plural feminine words that are not broken plurals (مؤنث سالم جمع), e.g. مُؤْمِنَاتٌ، طَالِبَاتٌ، صَالِحَاتٌ.
4. at the end of singular nouns when the letter before does not have a fatha, e.g. زَيْتٌ، ثَابِتٌ، تَفَاوُتٌ.

translateToArabic.ar: ثُمَّ أَعْطَتْهَا زَهْرَةً وَقَالَتْ: خُذِيْ هٰذِهِ وَشُمِّيْ

translateToEnglish.en: Faatimah says to Zainab

translateToEnglish.ar: سَمِعْتُ صَوْتَكِ، وَأَنْتِ تَقْرَئِيْنَ الْقُرْآنَ، فَفَرِحْتُ
translateToEnglish.en: I heard your voice while you were reciting the Qur'an, so I was delighted
Your voice is beautiful
and your recitation is beautiful
Sa'eedah took a flower from her classmate

translateToEnglish.ar: وَشَمَّتْ وَقَالَتْ: رَائِحَتُهَا طَيِّبَةٌ وَهِيَ جَمِيْلَةٌ
translateToEnglish.en: and she smelled it and said: Its fragrance is pleasant and it is beautiful

sentences.en: He gets up early in the morning
and he makes wudhu and performs salaah in the masjid
and he recites the Noble Qur'an
and he greets his mother and his father
and he goes to the school
He studies in the first class
and he listens to the teacher

sentences.ar: وَلَا يَلْتَفِتُ إِلَى الْيَمِيْنِ، أَوِ الْيَسَارِ
sentences.en: and he does not look to the right or to the left

translateToArabic.en: This is a pious man. He performs his salaah regularly and does his work truthfully and honestly
translateToArabic.ar: هٰذَا رَجُلٌ صَالِحٌ، يُوَاظِبُ عَلَى صَلَاتِهِ، وَيَعْمَلُ عَمَلَهُ بِصِدْقٍ وَأَمَانَةٍ

translateToArabic.en: He opens the classroom doors early in the morning, cleans them and then wails the siren
translateToArabic.ar: يَفْتَحُ أَبْوَابَ الْفُصُوْلِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ الْبَاكِرِ، وَيُنَظِّفُهَا، ثُمَّ يَدُقُّ الْجَرَسَ

translateToArabic.en: He locks the doors every evening
He serves the school with sincerity each day and night
translateToArabic.ar: يَخْدِمُ الْمَدْرَسَةَ بِإِخْلَاصٍ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ وَلَيْلَةٍ

translateToEnglish.en: Mahmood is an active boy
He takes the basket in the morning
and he goes out of the house

translateToEnglish.ar: وَيَذْهَبُ إِلَى سُوْقِ اللَّحْمِ فَيَشْتَرِي لَحْمًا
translateToEnglish.en: and he goes to the meat market and buys meat

translateToEnglish.ar: ثُمَّ يَذْهَبُ إِلَى سُوْقِ الْخُضْرَوَاتِ فَيَشْتَرِي خَضْرَةً وَفَاكِهَةً
translateToEnglish.en: then he goes to the vegetable market and buys vegetables and fruit
and he puts them in the basket

translateToEnglish.ar: ثُمَّ يَرْجِعُ إِلَى بَيْتِهِ وَيَتَنَاوَلُ الْفَطُوْرَ وَيَشْرَبُ الْحَلِيْبَ
translateToEnglish.en: then he returns to his house, eats breakfast and drinks the milk
then he goes to the school

vocabulary.en: The two of them are making Dhikr
The two of them are rehearsing
The two of them are studying

sentences.en: Khaalid and Shaahid are two brothers
They are two pupils in the school
They get up early in the morning
and they perform salaah in the masjid
and they recite the Noble Qur'an
and they greet their mother and their father
and they go to the school
The two of them study in the first class
and they listen to the teacher

sentences.ar: وَلَا يَلْتَفِتَانِ إِلَى الْيَمِيْنِ أَوِ الْيَسَارِ
sentences.en: and they do not look to the right or to the left

translateToArabic.en: Aabid and Aarif are two brothers
They are both pious and intelligent boys
They leave home early in the morning, go to the Masjid and perform salaah in Jamaa'ah
translateToArabic.ar: يَخْرُجَانِ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ الْبَاكِرِ، وَيَذْهَبَانِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ، وَيُصَلِّيَانِ مَعَ الْجَمَاعَةِ

translateToArabic.en: They then sit respectfully and make Dhikr
They then return home after a while, have their breakfast and go to school
translateToArabic.ar: ثُمَّ يَرْجِعَانِ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ بَعْدَ قَلِيْلٍ، وَيَتَنَاوَلَانِ الْفَطُوْرَ، وَيَذْهَبَانِ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ

translateToEnglish.en: Mahmood and I are two brothers
We study in the first class
We return from the school to the house
and we greet our father and our mother
and we eat the food
and we rest a little

translateToEnglish.ar: وَنَلْعَبُ ثُمَّ نَجْلِسُ وَنَقْرَأُ دُرُوسَنَا وَنَحْفَظُهَا
translateToEnglish.en: and we play, then we sit and read our lessons and memorise them

translateToEnglish.ar: وَعِنْدَ مَا يَأْتِي وَقْتُ الصَّلٰوةِ نَضَعُ الْكُتُبَ وَنَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ
translateToEnglish.en: and when the time of salaah comes we put down the books and go to the masjid
and we perform salaah with the congregation

notesEn: The Rule: to convert a singular مضارع verb to the dual form, simply add the letters (ان) at the end, e.g. تَذْهَبُ becomes تَذْهَبَانِ and يَدْخُلُ becomes يَدْخُلَانِ.

sentences.en: Khaalid, Shaahid and Sa'eed are brothers
They are pupils in the school
They get up early in the morning
and they perform salaah in the masjid
and they recite the Noble Qur'an
and they greet their mother and their father
and they go to the school
They study in the first class
and they listen to the teacher

sentences.ar: وَلَا يَلْتَفِتُوْنَ إِلَى الْيَمِيْنِ أَوِ الْيَسَارِ
sentences.en: and they do not look to the right or to the left

qaPairs.questionAr: مَنْ أَنْتُمْ يَا خَالِدُ وَشَاهِدُ وَسَعِيْدُ؟

translateToArabic.en: These are the students of the school
They come to school early in the morning and learn their lessons. They are hard working.
translateToArabic.ar: يَأْتُوْنَ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ الْبَاكِرِ وَيَتَعَلَّمُوْنَ دُرُوْسَهُمْ، هُمْ مُجْتَهِدُوْنَ

translateToArabic.en: They go home only in Ramadhaan
translateToArabic.ar: لَا يَذْهَبُوْنَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ إِلَّا فِي رَمَضَانَ

translateToEnglish.en: Today is Friday

translateToEnglish.ar: نَحْنُ لَا نَذْهَبُ الْيَوْمَ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ
translateToEnglish.en: We do not go to the school today
Today we bathe
and we put on clean clothes

translateToEnglish.ar: وَنَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْجَامِعِ وَنُصَلِّي الْجُمُعَةَ
translateToEnglish.en: and we go to the Jaami' Masjid and perform the Jumu'ah salaah
then we return to the house

translateToEnglish.ar: وَنَذْهَبُ إِلَى زُمَلَائِنَا وَنَزُوْرُهُمْ وَنُسَلِّمُ عَلَيْهِمْ
translateToEnglish.en: and we go to our companions and visit them and greet them
and we sit together
and we talk, then we return to the house

notesEn: The Rule: to convert a singular مضارع verb to the plural form, simply add the letters (ون) at the end, e.g. يَذْهَبُ becomes يَذْهَبُوْنَ and تَجْلِسُ becomes تَجْلِسُوْنَ.
The Rule: to convert a singular مضارع verb to the (first person) speaker form, simply add the letter (ن) at the beginning, e.g. نَكْتُبُ, نَذْهَبُ.
Exercise item omitted: "They do not go home, but stay in hostel" — the book gives no Arabic word for "hostel" anywhere in the lessons, so no confident answer could be supplied.

vocabulary.en: They do not dispute with each other

sentences.ar: لَعِبَتِ الطِّفْلَةُ مَعَ أُخْتِهَا فِي حَدِيْقَةِ الْمَنْزِلِ
sentences.en: The little girl played with her sister in the garden of the house

sentences.ar: جَهَّزَتِ الْأُمُّ الطَّعَامَ وَقَدَّمَتْهُ إِلَى أَوْلَادِهَا
sentences.en: The mother prepared the food and presented it to her children
Shaahid's father is a pious man
He gets up before the adhaan of Fajr
and he performs the Tahajjud salaah

sentences.ar: وَعِنْدَ مَا يَسْمَعُ أَذَانَ الْفَجْرِ يَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ
sentences.en: and when he hears the adhaan of Fajr he goes to the masjid
and he waits for the salaah
then he performs the Fajr salaah with the congregation
These are hard-working and pious students
They love their companions and their teachers
and they serve their mothers and their fathers
They do not lie and they do not dispute with one another

notesEn: The lesson is on dictation (أَلْإِمْلَاءُ): the Arabic side gives a list of single words (أَلْمُفْرَدَاتُ) and then sentences (أَلْجُمَلُ) to be written from dictation.

Some Principles of Dictation, 1: If the Hamzah wasl (الف الوصل) appears at the beginning of a sentence it is read and takes a harakat — ( اَ، اِ، اُ ) — e.g. أَلْكِتَابُ مُفِيْدٌ، أُكْتُبْ اسْمَكَ، اِجْلِسْ عَلَى الْكُرْسِيِّ. However, if another word comes before it, it is not read and does not take a harakat, e.g. إِنَّ الْكِتَابَ مُفِيْدٌ، وَاكْتُبْ اسْمَكَ، وَاجْلِسْ عَلَى الْكُرْسِيِّ. (The book prints "will to receive a Harkat", clearly a misprint for "will not receive a Harkat".)

Some Principles of Dictation, 2: If the Aliful qat' (ألف القطع) appears at the beginning of a sentence, the fatha or dhammah appears with a hamza ( أ ) on top of the alif, e.g. أُمٌّ، أَبٌ. If it has a kasra, the hamza appears at the bottom ( إ ), e.g. إِلَى، إِمْلَاء.

Dictation word list (أَلْمُفْرَدَاتُ) printed in this lesson: سَمِعْتُ، أَلْأَذَان، فَكَّرْتُ، تَكَلَّمْتُ، نَشِيْطٌ، يُصَلِّي، يَتْلُوْ، يَسْتَمِعُ، يَعُوْدُ، أَلْعِشَاءُ، أَنَامُ، أُمُّهُمَا، أَبُوْهُمَا، أَلْفَصْلُ، أَلْيَمِيْنُ، أَلْيَسَارُ، يَلْتَفِتُوْنَ، تُذَاكِرُوْنَ، أَوْ، إِلَى، أَيُّ.

sentences.ar: يَسْأَلُ الْأُسْتَاذُ خَالِدًا، مَاذَا فَعَلْتَ فِي الصَّبَاحِ؟ فَيُجِيْبُ خَالِدٌ وَيَقُوْلُ: يَا سَيِّدِيْ!
sentences.en: The teacher asks Khaalid: what did you do in the morning? So Khaalid replies and says: O my master!
I got up early in the morning
and I made wudhu and went to the masjid
and I performed the Fajr salaah with the congregation
and I recited the Noble Qur'an
then I returned to the house
and I ate breakfast and took my books

sentences.ar: وَسَلَّمْتُ عَلَى أَبِيْ وَأُمِّيْ وَجِئْتُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ
sentences.en: and I greeted my father and my mother and came to the school

sentences.ar: يَقُوْلُ مَحْمُوْدٌ: خَالِدٌ قَامَ فِي الصَّبَاحِ الْبَاكِرِ
sentences.en: Mahmood says: Khaalid got up early in the morning
and he made wudhu and went to the masjid
and he performed the Fajr salaah with the congregation
then he returned to the house
and he ate breakfast and took the books
and he greeted his father and his mother
and he came to the school

qaPairs.questionAr: يَا مَحْمُوْدُ! مَتَى قُمْتَ فِي الصَّبَاحِ؟

translateToArabic.en: The janitor opened the classrooms and cleaned them
He then sounded the siren and sat in the office
translateToArabic.ar: ثُمَّ دَقَّ الْجَرَسَ وَجَلَسَ فِي الْمَكْتَبِ

translateToEnglish.en: Khaalid went to the masjid
Mahmood sat beneath the trees
I came from the house
I wrote the letter
I took a pen
What did you eat, O Haamid?
And what did you drink?
I performed the Zuhr salaah in the masjid
I greeted my teacher
And I sat in my place

notesEn: The Rule: when the فعل مَاضِي of a three letter verb is to be determined from the مضارع verb, it may be done by removing the signs by which the مضارع verb is recognised and then adding a fatha to the first and third letters, e.g. يَذْهَبُ to ذَهَبَ and يَجْلِسُ to جَلَسَ; the singular form of the masculine third person is derived in this way.
The Rule: to derive the singular second, masculine person form of the verb, add the letter (تَ) to the end of the word.
The Rule: to derive the singular speaker form of the verb, add the letter (تُ) to the end of the word, e.g. ذَهَبَ to ذَهَبْتُ and ذَهَبْتَ etc.

sentences.ar: يَسْأَلُ الْأُسْتَاذُ خَالِدًا وَمَحْمُوْدًا: مَاذَا فَعَلْتُمَا فِي الصَّبَاحِ؟ فَيَقُوْلَانِ: يَا سَيِّدَنَا!
sentences.en: The teacher asks Khaalid and Mahmood: what did you two do in the morning? So they both say: O our master!
We got up early in the morning
and we went to the masjid
and we performed the Fajr salaah with the congregation
and we recited the Noble Qur'an

sentences.ar: ثُمَّ رَجَعْنَا إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَتَنَاوَلْنَا الْفَطُوْرَ
sentences.en: then we returned to the house and ate breakfast

sentences.ar: وَسَلَّمْنَا عَلَى أُمِّنَا وَأَبِيْنَا وَجِئْنَا إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ
sentences.en: and we greeted our mother and our father and came to the school

sentences.ar: يَقُوْلُ سَعِيْدٌ: قَامَ خَالِدٌ وَمَحْمُوْدٌ فِي الصَّبَاحِ
sentences.en: Sa'eed says: Khaalid and Mahmood got up in the morning
and they went to the masjid
and they performed the Fajr salaah with the congregation
and they recited the Noble Qur'an
then they returned to the house
and they came to the school

translateToArabic.en: He went to the marketplace today
They bought books and exercise books
Did you learn your lesson, Khaalid and Shaahid?
translateToArabic.ar: هَلْ حَفِظْتُمَا دَرْسَكُمَا يَا خَالِدُ وَشَاهِدُ؟

translateToArabic.en: We wrote it in our exercise books and understood it

translateToEnglish.en: The two students went to the field
and they played with the classmates
then they returned to the house
and they ate the food and slept

translateToEnglish.ar: أَنَا وَخَالِدٌ ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ، وَصَلَّيْنَا الْعِشَاءَ، ثُمَّ رَجَعْنَا إِلَى الْبَيْتِ
translateToEnglish.en: Khaalid and I went to the masjid, and we performed the Ishaa salaah, then we returned to the house

translateToEnglish.ar: أَيْنَ ذَهَبْتُمَا يَا خَالِدُ وَحَامِدُ، وَمَتَى رَجَعْتُمَا مِنَ الْمَدْرَسَةِ؟
translateToEnglish.en: Where did you two go, O Khaalid and Haamid, and when did you two return from the school?
Did you two see Shaahid?

notesEn: The Rule: When the letter ( ا ) is added to the end of the singular, masculine third person of the فعل ماضي verb, the verb becomes dual masculine third person, e.g. ذَهَبَ to ذَهَبَا، كَتَبَ to كَتَبَا etc.

The Rule: To convert the singular, feminine third person of the فعل مَاضِي verb into the dual feminine third person, add the letters تُمَا to the end, e.g. ذَهَبْتَ to ذَهَبْتُمَا، كَتَبْتَ to كَتَبْتُمَا.

The Rule: To form the speaker form of the فعل مَاضِي verb, simply add the letter تُ to the end, e.g. ذَهَبْنَا، كَتَبْنَا. Note that this form of the verb applies equally to masculine, feminine, singular, dual and plural. (The book prints the letter as تُ but gives نَا examples.)

sentences.ar: يَسْأَلُ الْأُسْتَاذُ الطُّلَّابَ: مَاذَا فَعَلْتُمْ فِي الصَّبَاحِ؟ فَيَقُوْلُوْنَ:
sentences.en: The teacher asks the students: what did you do in the morning? So they say:
We got up early in the morning
and we went to the masjid
and we performed the Fajr salaah with the congregation
and we recited the Noble Qur'an

sentences.ar: ثُمَّ رَجَعْنَا إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَتَنَاوَلْنَا الْفَطُوْرَ
sentences.en: then we returned to the house and ate breakfast
and we greeted our father and our mother
and we came to the school

sentences.ar: يَقُوْلُ سَعِيْدٌ: أَلطُّلَّابُ قَامُوْا فِي الصَّبَاحِ الْبَاكِرِ
sentences.en: Sa'eed says: The students got up early in the morning
and they went to the masjid
and they performed salaah with the congregation
and they recited the Noble Qur'an
then they returned to the house
and they came to the school

translateToArabic.en: The students sat in the classroom
We listened to the Jumu'ah Khutbah and performed the Jumu'ah salaah
Did you see the ocean, children?
Have you ever travelled by sea?
Have you ever seen an aeroplane?

translateToEnglish.ar: أَلطُّلَّابُ لَعِبُوْا فِي الْمَيْدَانِ، ثُمَّ رَجَعُوْا إِلَى بُيُوْتِهِمْ
translateToEnglish.en: The students played in the field, then they returned to their houses
The children ate and slept
We went to the marketplace and bought books
O children! Have you learnt the lesson?
And have you written the lesson?
Have you visited Lahore?
And have you seen the Royal Masjid?

notesEn: The Rule: To convert the singular, masculine third person of the فعل مَاضِي verb into the plural, add the letters ( وا ) to the end and add a Dhamma to the letter preceding the وَ, e.g. ذَهَبَ to ذَهَبُوْا.
The Rule: The ( ا ) at the end is not pronounced, even though it is written.
The Rule: To convert the singular, masculine second person of the فعل مَاضِي verb into the plural, add the letters تُم to the end, e.g. ذَهَبَ to ذَهَبْتُمْ etc.

sentences.en: She gets up early in the morning
and she performs salaah at home
and she recites the Noble Qur'an
and she greets her mother and her father
and she goes to the school
Aaishah returns from the school in the evening
and she helps her with the affairs of the house
then she plays with her sister
then she eats her food and sleeps early

translateToArabic.en: Sa'eeda says, "I am a little girl"
I am a student in the school
I read my lesson, learn it and then write it in my exercise book
translateToArabic.ar: أَقْرَأُ دَرْسِيْ وَأَحْفَظُهُ ثُمَّ أَكْتُبُهُ فِي كُرَّاسَتِيْ

translateToArabic.en: My teacher likes me a lot and I like her as well
translateToArabic.ar: مُعَلِّمَتِيْ تُحِبُّنِيْ كَثِيْرًا وَأَنَا أُحِبُّهَا أَيْضًا

translateToArabic.en: I sit before her with respect
I play with her and do not hit her

translateToEnglish.en: The mother says to her daughter: O my dear little daughter!
Wake up early in the morning
and make wudhu
and perform the Fajr salaah at home
and recite the Noble Qur'an

translateToEnglish.ar: ثُمَّ اذْهَبِيْ إِلَى وَالِدِكِ وَسَلِّمِيْ عَلَيْهِ
translateToEnglish.en: Then go to your father and greet him with Salaam

translateToEnglish.ar: اشْرَبِي الْحَلِيْبَ، خُذِي الْكُتُبَ، وَاذْهَبِيْ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ
translateToEnglish.en: Drink the milk, take the books, and go to the school

translateToEnglish.ar: أُدْخُلِيْ فَصْلَكِ وَسَلِّمِيْ عَلَى مُعَلِّمَتِكِ وَزَمِيْلَاتِكِ
translateToEnglish.en: Enter your classroom and greet your teacher and your classmates with Salaam
And sit with respect, and read your lessons

sentences.en: Aaishah and Faatimah are two sisters
They get up early in the morning
and they make wudhu and perform salaah at home
and they recite the Noble Qur'an
then they eat breakfast and take the books
and they greet their mother and their father
and they go to the school

sentences.ar: تَرْجِعُ عَائِشَةُ وَفَاطِمَةُ مِنَ الْمَدْرَسَةِ فِي الْمَسَاءِ
sentences.en: Aaishah and Faatimah return from the school in the evening
and they help her with the affairs of the house
and they play with their sister a little

translateToArabic.en: Sa'eeda and Zaynab say, "We are students in the school"
translateToArabic.ar: تَقُوْلُ سَعِيْدَةُ وَزَيْنَبُ: نَحْنُ تِلْمِيْذَتَانِ فِي الْمَدْرَسَةِ

translateToArabic.en: We read our lessons, learn them and then write them in our exercise books
translateToArabic.ar: نَقْرَأُ دُرُوْسَنَا وَنَحْفَظُهَا ثُمَّ نَكْتُبُهَا فِي كُرَّاسَتَيْنَا

translateToArabic.en: Our teacher likes us a lot and we like her as well
translateToArabic.ar: مُعَلِّمَتُنَا تُحِبُّنَا كَثِيْرًا وَنَحْنُ نُحِبُّهَا أَيْضًا

translateToArabic.en: We play with her, do not hit her and we love her a great deal
translateToArabic.ar: نَلْعَبُ مَعَهَا وَلَا نَضْرِبُهَا، بَلْ نُحِبُّهَا كَثِيْرًا

translateToEnglish.ar: أَلْمُعَلِّمَةُ تَقُوْلُ لِعَائِشَةَ وَفَاطِمَةَ: اسْتَيْقِظَا فِي الصَّبَاحِ الْبَاكِرِ
translateToEnglish.en: The teacher says to Aaishah and Faatimah: Wake up early in the morning
and perform the Fajr salaah
then read the Noble Qur'an

translateToEnglish.ar: اذْهَبَا إِلَى أُمِّكُمَا وَسَلِّمَا عَلَيْهَا، وَاشْرَبَا الْحَلِيْبَ وَلَا تَشْرَبَا الشَّايَ
translateToEnglish.en: Go to your mother and greet her with Salaam, and drink the milk and do not drink the tea

translateToEnglish.ar: خُذَا كُتُبَكُمَا وَتَعَالَيَا إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ، وَاجْلِسَا بِأَدَبٍ
translateToEnglish.en: Take your books and come to the school, and sit with respect

translateToEnglish.ar: وَاقْرَءَا دَرْسَكُمَا وَاحْفَظَاهُ، ثُمَّ اكْتُبَاهُ فِي الْكُرَّاسَةِ
translateToEnglish.en: And read your lesson and learn it, then write it in the exercise book

notesEn: The Rule: When converting the present and future tense verbs from singular to dual, the procedure to be followed is to add the letters ( ان ) to the end of the singular verb, e.g. تَذْهَبُ to تَذْهَبَانِ and تَذْهَبِيْنَ to تَذْهَبَانِ.
The Rule: This applies equally to the verb with the second person as the doer as well as the verb with the third person as the doer, e.g. نَذْهَبُ، نَجْلِسُ etc.

sentences.en: They get up early in the morning
and they make wudhu and perform salaah at home
and they recite the Noble Qur'an
And they greet their mother and their father
and they go to the school
and they return from the school in the evening
and they help her with the affairs of the house
And they play with their little sister

translateToArabic.en: The teacher enters the classroom and says to the students, "Be quiet girls and sit in your places"
translateToArabic.ar: تَدْخُلُ الْمُعَلِّمَةُ الْفَصْلَ وَتَقُوْلُ لِلطَّالِبَاتِ: اُسْكُتْنَ يَا بَنَاتُ وَاجْلِسْنَ فِي أَمَاكِنِكُنَّ

translateToArabic.en: Open your books, read the lesson and learn it
Then write it down in your exercise books
The lesson is now over. You may go home
translateToArabic.ar: اِنْتَهَى الدَّرْسُ الْآنَ، اِذْهَبْنَ إِلَى بُيُوْتِكُنَّ

translateToArabic.en: Walk with respect and do not play on the roads
translateToArabic.ar: اِمْشِيْنَ بِأَدَبٍ وَلَا تَلْعَبْنَ فِي الطَّرِيْقِ

translateToArabic.en: Greet your mothers with Salaam and then help them with the housework
translateToArabic.ar: سَلِّمْنَ عَلَى أُمَّهَاتِكُنَّ ثُمَّ سَاعِدْنَهُنَّ فِي أُمُوْرِ الْمَنْزِلِ

translateToArabic.en: The mothers are rearing their children
We are learning our lesson and writing it down
We perform salaah, fast and serve our mothers
Those girls veil themselves and do good deeds

translateToEnglish.en: The mothers love their children
The little girls are playing in the garden of the house

translateToEnglish.ar: أَلطَّالِبَاتُ يَتَكَلَّمْنَ فِي مَا بَيْنَهُنَّ وَيَضْحَكْنَ
translateToEnglish.en: The (female) students are speaking among themselves and laughing

translateToEnglish.ar: أَلْمُعَلِّمَاتُ يَسْأَلْنَ الطَّالِبَاتِ: عَمَّا تَتَكَلَّمْنَ؟ وَلِمَاذَا تَضْحَكْنَ؟
translateToEnglish.en: The (female) teachers ask the students: what are you speaking about? And why are you laughing?

translateToEnglish.ar: أُدْخُلْنَ الْفَصْلَ وَاجْلِسْنَ بِأَدَبٍ، وَاقْرَأْنَ دُرُوْسَكُنَّ، وَاحْفَظْنَهَا
translateToEnglish.en: Enter the classroom and sit with respect, and read your lessons, and learn them

notesEn: The Rule: To form the plural feminine verb of the third person in the present and future tense, add the letter ( نَ ) to the singular masculine form of the verb also of the third person, e.g. يَذْهَبُ to يَذْهَبْنَ etc.

The Rule: To form the plural feminine verb of the second person in the present and future tense, add the letter ( نَ ) to the singular masculine form of the verb also of the second person, e.g. تَذْهَبُ to تَذْهَبْنَ.

Exercise 2 (أَكْمِلِ الْجُمَلَ النَّاقِصَةِ ثُمَّ تَرْجِمْهَا بِالإِنْجِلِيْزِيَّةِ, book page 131) is a fill-in-the-blank drill: a singular sentence is printed and the learner completes the dual and plural columns — أَلْبِنْتُ تَلْعَبُ / أَلْبِنْتَانِ ... / أَلْبَنَاتُ ...، أَلطَّالِبَةُ تَفْهَمُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ / أَلطَّالِبَتَانِ ... / أَلطَّالِبَاتُ ...، أَلْمَرْأَةُ تُصَلِّي / أَلْمَرْأَتَانِ ... / أَلنِّسَاءُ ...، أَلْمُعَلِّمَةُ تُدَرِّسُ / أَلْمُعَلِّمَتَانِ ... / أَلْمُعَلِّمَاتُ ...، أَنْتِ تَكْتُبِيْنَ / أَنْتُمَا ... / أَنْتُنَّ ...، أَلْفَتَاةُ صَالِحَةٌ / أَلْفَتَاتَانِ ... / أَلْفَتَيَاتُ ...، أَلْمَرْأَةُ مُحْتَجِبَةٌ / أَلْمَرْأَتَانِ ... / أَلنِّسَاءُ ....

sentences.en: The diligent female student guards her time

sentences.ar: وَتَصْرِفُهَا فِي الدِّرَاسَةِ وَالْمُطَالَعَةِ، وَالْمُذَاكِرَةِ وَالْحِفْظِ
sentences.en: and she spends it in study and reading, and in revision and memorisation
The two female students went to the school
then they went to the notice board

sentences.ar: عَلَى جَمِيْعِ الطَّالِبَاتِ أَنْ يَجْتَمِعْنَ فِي قَاعَةِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ السَّاعَةَ الْعَاشِرَةَ
sentences.en: All the female students must gather in the school hall at ten o'clock
Excellent female teachers will attend the gathering
and they will address the students
and advise them with good advice
The two female students were delighted at reading this announcement

sentences.ar: وَقَالَتَا: سَنَحْضُرُ هٰذَا الْاِجْتِمَاعَ إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ تَعَالَى
sentences.en: and they said: We shall attend this gathering, if Allah Ta'aala wills

notesEn: Some Principles of Dictation: The following are the principles to be followed when writting the Hamzah Mautawassita ( هَمْزَة مُتَوَسِّطَة ), which is the ألف القطع that appears between a word:
1. If it follows the letter ( ي ) with a Sukoon on it, the Hamzah will be written above a little line, e.g. هَيْئَةَ، بِيْئَةَ، هٰذَا شَيْئُكَ etc.
2. If it follows the letter ( و ) with a Sukoon on it, the Hamzah will be written separately, e.g. وُضُوْءُكَ، ضَوْءُكَ، تَوْءَمُ etc.
3. If it follows the letter ( ا ) with a Sukoon on it, the Hamzah will again be written separately, e.g. تَفَاءَلَ، خُذْ رِدَاءَكَ، هُمَا جَاءَا etc.

4. If it follows a letter with a Harkat on it, the Hamzah will be written in the form that resembles the Harkat of the letter, i.e. it will be written as the letter ( ا ) when the preceding letter has a Fatha ( رَأْيُ ), it will be written as the letter ( ي ) when the preceding letter has a Kasra ( بِئْرٌ، ذِئْبٌ ) and it will be written as the letter ( و ) when the preceding letter has a Dhamma ( سُؤْلُ ) etc.
5. If the هَمْزَة مُتَوَسِّطَة has a Kasra beneath it, it will always be written as ي, e.g. أَسْئِلَةٌ، سُئِلَ، مَسَائِلُ.

The lesson opens with a dictation word list headed أَلْمُفْرَدَاتُ (no English is printed with it): أُخْتُ، تَتْلُو، تَأْخُذُ، أُمُّهُمَا، أَبُوْهُمَا، أُمُوْرٌ، تَقْرَءَانِ، صَبَاحًا، مَسَاءً، نَقْرَأُ، يَقُمْنَ، يَتَوَضَّأْنَ، يُسَلِّمْنَ، يَأْكُلْنَ، يَقْرَأْنَ، يَنَمْنَ.

sentences.ar: تَسْأَلُ الْمُعَلِّمَةُ فَاطِمَةَ، مَاذَا فَعَلْتِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ؟
sentences.en: The teacher asks Faatima: what did you do in the morning?
So she says: I got up in the morning and performed wudu
and I prayed Fajr at home
and I recited the Noble Qur'aan

sentences.ar: تَقُولُ زَيْنَبُ: فَاطِمَةُ قَامَتْ فِي الصَّبَاحِ الْبَاكِرِ
sentences.en: Zainab says: Faatima got up early in the morning
and she performed wudu and prayed Fajr at home
and she recited the Noble Qur'aan
and she greeted her father and her mother

translateToArabic.en: Faatima said to her mother: Dear mother!
I did not go to school
I woke up early in the morning
and my sister cleaned the room
Where were you in the morning, Sa'eeda?
translateToArabic.ar: أَيْنَ كُنْتِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ يَا سَعِيدَةُ؟

translateToEnglish.ar: أَخَذَتْ فَاطِمَةُ الْجَرِيدَةَ وَقَرَأَتْ ثُمَّ وَضَعَتِ الْجَرِيدَةَ عَلَى الْمَكْتَبِ.
translateToEnglish.en: Faatima took the newspaper and read it, then she put the newspaper on the desk.
I got up in the morning, and I opened the windows.

translateToEnglish.ar: يَازَيْنَبُ! هَلْ فَهِمْتِ الدَّرْسَ؟ وَهَلْ كَتَبْتِ الرِّسَالَةَ إِلَى أَبِيكِ؟
translateToEnglish.en: O Zainab! Did you understand the lesson? And did you write the letter to your father?

translateToEnglish.ar: الطِّفْلَةُ أَكَلَتْ وَشَرِبَتْ وَلَعِبَتْ ثُمَّ نَامَتْ.
translateToEnglish.en: The little girl ate and drank and played, then she slept.

notesEn: The Rule: To convert the singular, masculine third person of the fi'l maadi (فعل مَاضِي) verb into the singular feminine third person, add the letter ت to the end, e.g. ذَهَبَ to ذَهَبَتْ and أَخَذَ to أَخَذَتْ.

The Rule: To convert the singular, masculine third person of the fi'l maadi verb into the singular feminine second person, add the letter تِ to the end and add a Sukoon to the preceding letter, e.g. ذَهَبَ to ذَهَبْتِ etc.
The Rule: To convert the singular, masculine third person of the fi'l maadi verb into the singular speaker (first person), add the letter تُ to the end, e.g. ذَهَبَ to ذَهَبْتُ.

lessons.topicEn: Fi'l Maadi, the two female students

sentences.en: Faatima and Zainab are going to school

sentences.ar: فَتَسْأَلُهُمَا الْمُعَلِّمَةُ: مَاذَا فَعَلْتُمَا فِي الصَّبَاحِ؟
sentences.en: so the teacher asks them both: What did you two do in the morning?
So they both say: We got up early in the morning
and we prayed Fajr at home
and we recited the Noble Qur'aan
and we greeted our father and our mother

sentences.ar: ثُمَّ تَسْأَلُ الْمُعَلِّمَةُ طَالِبَةً: مَاذَا فَعَلَتْ فَاطِمَةُ وَزَيْنَبُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ؟
sentences.en: Then the teacher asks a female student: What did Faatima and Zainab do in the morning?

sentences.ar: فَتُجِيبُ: فَاطِمَةُ وَزَيْنَبُ قَامَتَا فِي الصَّبَاحِ الْبَاكِرِ
sentences.en: So she answers: Faatima and Zainab both got up early in the morning
and they both prayed Fajr at home
then they both recited the Noble Qur'aan
and they both took the books

sentences.ar: وَسَلَّمَتَا عَلَى أَبِيهِمَا وَأُمِّهِمَا وَجَاءَتَا إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ
sentences.en: and they both greeted their father and their mother and they both came to school

translateToEnglish.ar: الطَّالِبَتَانِ كَتَبَتَا عَلَى السَّبُّورَةِ، ثُمَّ مَسَحَتَا السَّبُّورَةَ بِالطَّلَّاسَةِ.
translateToEnglish.en: The two (female) students wrote on the blackboard, then they both wiped the blackboard with the duster.

translateToEnglish.ar: مَاذَا كَتَبْتُمَا عَلَى السَّبُّورَةِ؟ كَتَبْنَا أَسْمَاءَنَا عَلَى السَّبُّورَةِ.
translateToEnglish.en: What did you two write on the blackboard? We wrote our names on the blackboard.
With what did you two wipe the blackboard? We wiped it with the duster.

translateToEnglish.ar: أَيْنَ وَضَعْتُمَا الطَّلَّاسَةَ؟ وَضَعْنَاهَا تَحْتَ السَّبُّورَةِ.
translateToEnglish.en: Where did you two put the duster? We put it under the blackboard.

translateToEnglish.ar: هَلْ حَفِظْتُمَا الدَّرْسَ؟ نَعَمْ حَفِظْنَاهُ، وَفَهِمْنَاهُ وَكَتَبْنَاهُ.
translateToEnglish.en: Did you two memorise the lesson? Yes, we memorised it, and we understood it and we wrote it.

notesEn: The Rule: To convert the singular fi'l maadi (فعل مَاضِي) verb into the dual, simply add the letter ا to the end, e.g. ذَهَبَتْ to ذَهَبَتَا. Remember that the letter preceding this ا will always have Fatha.
The Rule: The dual feminine of the second person will, however, receive the letters تُمَا at the end, e.g. ذَهَبْتُمَا. In this case, masculine and feminine will be the same.

Exercise 2 (كَوِّنِ الْمُثَنَّى مِنَ الْأَفْعَالِ الْآتِيَةِ): form the dual from the following verbs — ذَهَبَتْ ، رَجَعَتْ ، جَلَسَتْ ، نَامَتْ ، أَكَلَتْ ، شَرِبَتْ ، غَسَلَتْ ، فَرِحَتْ ، حَفِظَتْ ، فَهِمَتْ.

sentences.ar: تَسْأَلُ الْمُعَلِّمَةُ الطَّالِبَاتِ مَاذَا فَعَلْتُنَّ فِي الصَّبَاحِ؟
sentences.en: The teacher asks the (female) students: What did you all do in the morning?
So they say: We got up early in the morning
and we prayed Fajr at home
and we read the Noble Qur'aan

sentences.ar: وَسَلَّمْنَا عَلَى آبَائِنَا وَأُمَّهَاتِنَا وَجِئْنَا إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ.
sentences.en: and we greeted our fathers and our mothers and we came to school

sentences.ar: ثُمَّ تَسْأَلُ الْمُعَلِّمَةُ طَالِبَةً: مَاذَا فَعَلَتِ الطَّالِبَاتُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ؟
sentences.en: Then the teacher asks a female student: What did the female students do in the morning?

sentences.ar: فَتُجِيبُ: الطَّالِبَاتُ قُمْنَ فِي الصَّبَاحِ الْبَاكِرِ
sentences.en: So she answers: The students got up early in the morning
and they prayed Fajr at home
and they recited the Noble Qur'aan

sentences.ar: وَسَلَّمْنَ عَلَى آبَائِهِنَّ وَأُمَّهَاتِهِنَّ وَجِئْنَ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ.
sentences.en: and they greeted their fathers and their mothers and they came to school

translateToArabic.en: The women gathered in the house and starting talking to each other
translateToArabic.ar: النِّسَاءُ اجْتَمَعْنَ فِي الْبَيْتِ وَتَكَلَّمْنَ مَعَ بَعْضِهِنَّ

translateToArabic.en: The girls returned home from school
translateToArabic.ar: الْبَنَاتُ رَجَعْنَ مِنَ الْمَدْرَسَةِ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ

translateToArabic.en: They all drank milk and then helped their mother with the housework
translateToArabic.ar: شَرِبْنَ جَمِيعًا لَبَنًا ثُمَّ سَاعَدْنَ أُمَّهُنَّ فِي أَعْمَالِ الْبَيْتِ

translateToArabic.en: They played for a little while and then learnt their lessons
Their mother called them and gave them advice
The girls entered the school and sat in the classroom
translateToArabic.ar: الْبَنَاتُ دَخَلْنَ الْمَدْرَسَةَ وَجَلَسْنَ فِي الْفَصْلِ

translateToArabic.en: They told their teacher, "We have learnt our lesson and understand it well"
translateToArabic.ar: قُلْنَ لِمُعَلِّمَتِهِنَّ: حَفِظْنَا دَرْسَنَا وَفَهِمْنَاهُ جَيِّدًا

translateToArabic.en: The girls left the house and entered the garden, played for awhile and they returned home
translateToArabic.ar: الْبَنَاتُ خَرَجْنَ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ وَدَخَلْنَ الْحَدِيقَةَ، وَلَعِبْنَ قَلِيلًا ثُمَّ رَجَعْنَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ

translateToArabic.en: They ate their food and went to sleep

translateToEnglish.en: The women gathered in the house.
The mothers nursed their children.

translateToEnglish.ar: الطَّالِبَاتُ سَلَّمْنَ عَلَى مُعَلِّمَتِهِنَّ، وَالْمُعَلِّمَاتُ عَلَّمْنَ الطَّالِبَاتِ.
translateToEnglish.en: The (female) students greeted their teacher, and the (female) teachers taught the students.

translateToEnglish.ar: قَالَتِ النِّسَاءُ الْمُسْلِمَاتُ: آمَنَّا بِاللهِ وَصَلَّيْنَا
translateToEnglish.en: The Muslim women said: We have believed in Allah and we prayed

and we paid the zakaah

notesEn: The Rule: To form the plural feminine verb of the third person in the past tense, add the letter (نَ) to the singular masculine form of the verb also of the third person, ensuring that the letter before it has a Sukoon, e.g. ذَهَبَ to ذَهَبْنَ.

The Rule: To form the plural feminine verb of the second person in the past tense, add the letters تُنَّ to the singular masculine form of the verb also of the second person, e.g. ذَهَبْتُنَّ، جِئْتُنَّ etc.

The Rule: Note that the plural feminine verb of the third person in the past tense is used only after a plural feminine noun of the third person, e.g. الطَّالِبَاتُ ذَهَبْنَ. However, if the verb appears before the noun, it will always be the singular feminine verb of the third person in the past tense, e.g. ذَهَبَتِ الطَّالِبَاتُ.

sentences.ar: هٰذَا بُسْتَانُ مَحْمُودٍ، نَدْخُلُ فِي الْبُسْتَانِ، نَمْشِي تَحْتَ الْأَشْجَارِ وَبَيْنَ الْأَزْهَارِ.
sentences.en: This is Mahmood's garden; we enter the garden, we walk under the trees and among the flowers.
We eat the fruits and we smell the flowers
The fruits are sweet and delicious
and the flowers are beautiful, and their fragrance is pleasant
We play on the green grass
and we sit on the benches and we talk
We hear the beautiful sounds of the birds

sentences.ar: ثُمَّ نَخْرُجُ مِنَ الْبُسْتَانِ، وَنَعُودُ إِلَى بُيُوتِنَا مَسْرُورِينَ.
sentences.en: Then we leave the garden, and we return to our homes happy.

translateToEnglish.en: The father says to his son: Dear son!
Go to the garden and play in it
and look at its trees and its flowers
and sit on its grass

translateToEnglish.ar: وَلَا تَقْطِفْ ثَمَرَةً وَلَا زَهْرَةً، وَلَا تَكْسِرْ غُصْنًا، وَلَا تَضْرِبْ أَحَدًا.
translateToEnglish.en: And do not pluck a fruit nor a flower, and do not break a branch, and do not hit anyone.

translateToEnglish.ar: وَامْشِ فِي الطَّرِيقِ وَانْظُرْ أَمَامَكَ وَلَا تَلْتَفِتْ يَمِينًا وَلَا يَسَارًا.
translateToEnglish.en: And walk on the road and look in front of you and do not turn to the right nor to the left.

sentences.en: Sa'eeda is a beautiful, intelligent little girl
She got up from her sleep
then she went to her mother
and she asked her: Where is my brother Haamid?

sentences.ar: فَقَالَتِ الْأُمُّ: هُوَ ذَهَبَ مَعَ وَالِدِهِ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ
sentences.en: So the mother said: He went with his father to the masjid

sentences.ar: الْمَرْأَةُ هِيَ: الْبِنْتُ، وَالْأُخْتُ، وَالْأُمُّ، وَالزَّوْجَةُ
sentences.en: The woman is: the daughter, and the sister, and the mother, and the wife
It is necessary to bring her up with a correct Islamic upbringing
so that her faith becomes strong
She knows the rights of the parents, because she is a daughter

sentences.ar: وَتَعْرِفُ حُقُوقَ إِخْوَتِهَا وَأَخَوَاتِهَا؛ لِأَنَّهَا أُخْتٌ
sentences.en: and she knows the rights of her brothers and her sisters, because she is a sister
and she knows the rights of her children, because she is a mother
and she knows the rights of her husband, because she is a wife

notesEn: This lesson is a dictation (أَلْإِمْلَاءُ) lesson. Under the heading أَلْمُفْرَدَاتُ (single words) the following words are listed for dictation practice: نَسْأَلُ ، تَوَضَّأْنَا ، قَرَأْنَا ، أَكَلْنَا ، رَأَيْتُنَّ ، تَوَضَّأْنَ ، جِئْنَ ، نَأْكُلُ ، أَصْوَاتٌ ، رَائِحَتُهَا ، قُمْتُنَّ ، أَخَذْنَ ، رَأَيْتُنَّ ، آبَاؤُهُنَّ ، أُمَّهَاتُهُنَّ.

Some Principles of Dictation (1): If a Hamzah with a Fatha (Hamzah Maftooha) is not followed by a letter of Madd (ا، و or ي), the Hamzah Maftooha will be written in the form that resembles the Harkat of the preceding letter, e.g. فِئَة، لُؤَى، سَأَل.

Some Principles of Dictation (2): If the letter preceding the Hamzah Maftooha is a proper (Sahih) letter and has a Sukoon, the Hamzah Maftooha will be written in the form of an Alif, e.g. يَسْأَل، مَسْأَلَةٌ.

Some Principles of Dictation (3): If the letter preceding the Hamzah Maftooha is a letter of Madd, one of the following will take place: (a) If both the letters before and after the Hamzah Maftooha are joined to it, the Hamzah Maftooha will be written upon a curve, e.g. مكافئات، ملجئان. (b) If the letters before and after the Hamzah Maftooha are not joined to it, the Hamzah Maftooha will be written as a separate Hamzah, e.g. جُزْءَان ، قَرَءَا ، يَقْرَءَان ، لَمْ يَقْرَءَا.

sentences.en: In the school there are eight classes
In the room there are seven students
On the field there are nine children
In the week there are seven days

translateToArabic.en: There are 10 men on the field
There are 6 boys in the garden
There are presently 9 students in the class room
There are 4 doors in the Masjid
There are 4 janitors in the school
There is 1 field in front of the school
I have 7 books in my hand

notesEn: The Rule: The following rules apply to the number and the items being counted up to ten.

The Rule: No number is used for one or two items. The singular word denotes one item and the dual word denotes two, e.g. كِتَاب and كِتَابَان. However, a number may be used after these forms to emphasise the number, e.g. عِنْدِي كِتَابٌ وَاحِدٌ، عِنْدِي كِتَابَانِ اثْنَانِ.

The Rule: From 3 to 10, the item being counted will always appear in the plural, with the last letter having a Kasra, e.g. عِنْدِي عَشَرَةُ كُتُبٍ. Furthermore, if the item being counted is masculine, the number will be feminine, e.g. أَرْبَعَةُ كُتُبٍ، خَمْسَةُ طُلَّابٍ.

sentences.en: There are three clocks in the school
There are two clocks in the mosque
There are five exercise books on the desk
There are ten female students in the class

translateToArabic.en: There are 10 bicycles in the store
There are 4 girls in the room
There are 7 aeroplanes at the airport
There are 2 ships at the harbour
There are only 8 hats at the shop

notesEn: The Rule: although the singular word denotes one item and the dual word denotes two, a number may be used after these forms to emphasise the number, e.g. عِنْدِيْ سَاعَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ، فِي الْمَسْجِدِ سَاعَتَانِ اثْنَتَانِ. Note that the feminine number is used for the feminine item being counted and masculine numbers will be used for masculine items.

The Rule: from 3 to 10 the item being counted will always appear in the plural, with the last letter having a Kasra. Furthermore, if the item being counted is feminine, the number will be masculine, e.g. ثَلَاثُ سَاعَاتٍ، عَشَرُ سَاعَاتٍ.

sentences.en: There are twenty students in the first class
and in the second there are twenty students
and in the third there are twelve students
There are sixteen children on the field
There are nineteen passengers in the bus
and in the car there are five passengers

translateToArabic.en: There are 11 passengers on the bus
There are 15 boys in the room
There are 20 boys on the field

translateToArabic.ar: هٰذِهِ ثَمَانِيَةَ عَشَرَ كِتَابًا وَسِتَّةَ عَشَرَ قَلَمًا

translateToArabic.en: There are 14 roads in this town
translateToArabic.ar: فِيْ هٰذَا الْبَلَدِ أَرْبَعَةَ عَشَرَ طَرِيْقًا

translateToArabic.en: There are 12 pillars in this street
translateToArabic.ar: فِيْ هٰذَا الشَّارِعِ اثْنَا عَشَرَ عَمُوْدًا
كَانَ خَالِدٌ مَرِيْضًا سَبْعَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا

notesEn: The Rule: as stated in the lesson, the numbers from 11 to 19 are always in pairs and the items counted are always in their singular form, with the last letter having a Fatha. This applies to all numbers until 99.

The Rule: when the item counted is masculine, the numbers 11 and 12 are also masculine, and when feminine, the numbers will be feminine as well, e.g. أَحَدَ عَشَرَ كِتَابًا and اثْنَا عَشَرَ كِتَابًا. However, when the numbers range from 13 to 19, the number will be masculine when the item being counted is feminine and vice versa, e.g. ثَلَاثَةَ عَشَرَ كِتَابًا.
The Rule: the tens from 20 to 90 will remain the same regardless of the gender of the items being counted, e.g. عِشْرُوْنَ سَاعَةً and عِشْرُوْنَ كِتَابًا.

Exercise 2 (أُكْتُبِ الْأَرْقَامَ بِالْحُرُوْفِ — write the figures out in words): nine short sentences each containing a figure from 11 to 20, e.g. فِي الْمِحْفَظَةِ ١١ كِتَابًا، فِي الْإِدَارَةِ ١٨ مُوَظَّفًا، فِي السِّجْنِ ١٣ مُجْرِمًا.

sentences.en: In it there are five grades
In the first grade there are twenty female students
and in the second there are fifteen female students
and in the third there are fourteen female students
and in the fourth there are twelve female students
and in the fifth there are ten female students

translateToArabic.en: There are 16 trees in the garden
There are 11 flowers on that branch
translateToArabic.ar: عَلَى ذٰلِكَ الْغُصْنِ إِحْدَى عَشَرَةَ زَهْرَةً

translateToArabic.en: There are 12 fowls in that house
translateToArabic.ar: فِيْ ذٰلِكَ الْبَيْتِ اثْنَتَا عَشَرَةَ دَجَاجَةً

translateToArabic.en: There are 18 eggs in that basket
translateToArabic.ar: فِيْ تِلْكَ السَّلَّةِ ثَمَانِيَ عَشَرَةَ بَيْضَةً

translateToArabic.en: There are 16 Rupees in my pocket

translateToArabic.ar: هٰذَا الْعَامِلُ يَعْمَلُ أَرْبَعَ عَشَرَةَ سَاعَةً
أَنَا حَاضِرٌ بَعْدَ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ يَوْمًا

translateToArabic.en: There are 19 rooms in this building
translateToArabic.ar: فِيْ هٰذِهِ الْبِنَايَةِ تِسْعَ عَشَرَةَ غُرْفَةً

notesEn: The Rule: as stated in the previous lesson, when the item counted is feminine, the numbers 11 and 12 are also feminine. However, when the numbers range from 13 to 19, the number will be masculine when the item being counted is feminine, e.g. ثَلَاثَ عَشَرَةَ سَاعَةً.
The Rule: again, the tens from 20 to 90 will remain the same regardless of the gender of the items being counted, e.g. عِشْرُوْنَ كِتَابًا and عِشْرُوْنَ سَاعَةً.
The Arabic term for the item being counted is the Tameez (تميز).

Exercise 2 (أُكْتُبِ الْأَرْقَامَ بِالْحُرُوْفِ — write the figures out in words): nine short sentences each containing a figure from 11 to 20 with a feminine counted noun, e.g. ثَمَنُ الْكِتَابِ ١١ رُوْبِيَّةً. فِي الْحَوْضِ ١٤ سَمَكَةً. عَلَى الشَّجَرَةِ ١٨ حَمَامَةً.

sentences.en: There are twenty-five pens in the box
There are thirty students in the class
There are twenty-eight passengers in the bus
There are twenty-two children on the field

translateToEnglish.en: There are thirty labourers in the factory
There are twenty-five passengers at the station
Twenty-one guests entered the hall
There are twenty-three books on the desk
The mosque has twenty-four doors
There are twenty-eight lecturers in the college

notesEn: The Rule 1: the Tameez in the numbers from 21 to 99 is always singular and Mansoob.

The Rule 2: the first two numbers after every ten (21 and 22, 31 and 32, etc) will be in the masculine form when the Tameez is masculine, e.g. وَاحِدٌ وَّعِشْرُوْنَ رَجُلًا and إِثْنَانِ وَعِشْرُوْنَ رَجُلًا.
The Rule 3: all the other numbers after the tens (23 to 29, 33 to 39, etc) will be feminine when the Tameez is masculine, e.g. ثَلَاثَةٌ وَّعِشْرُوْنَ كِتَابًا.
The Rule 4: remember that the tens themselves from 20 to 90 will remain the same regardless of the gender of the Tameez, e.g. ثَلَاثُوْنَ رَجُلًا and ثَلَاثُوْنَ امْرَأَةً.

Exercise 2 (أُكْتُبِ الْأَرْقَامَ بِالْحُرُوْفِ — write the figures out in words): eight figures from 21 to 30 with a masculine counted noun, ٢١ كِتَابًا، ٢٢ قَلَمًا، ٢٥ كُرْسِيًّا، ٢٣ بَابًا، ٢٦ وَلَدًا، ٢٨ رَجُلًا، ٢٤ تِلْمِيْذًا، ٣٠ مُدَرِّسًا.

sentences.en: There are thirty exercise books on the desk
There are twenty-five apples on the branch
There are twenty-two roses on the tree

There are twenty-seven trees in the garden

translateToEnglish.en: There are twenty-five female students in the class
There are thirty women in the hall
There are twenty-two little girls in the garden
There are twenty-one rupees in my pocket
There are twenty-three flowers in the vase
There are twenty-four pages in the exercise book

notesEn: The Rule 1: the Tameez in the numbers from 21 to 99 is always singular and Mansoob.

The Rule 2: the first two numbers after every ten (21 and 22, 31 and 32, etc) will be in the feminine form when the Tameez is feminine, e.g. إِحْدَى وَعِشْرُوْنَ سَاعَةً، اثْنَتَانِ وَعِشْرُوْنَ سَاعَةً.
The Rule 3: all the other numbers after the tens (23 to 29, 33 to 39, etc) will be masculine when the Tameez is feminine, e.g. ثَلَاثٌ وَّعِشْرُوْنَ سَاعَةً، تِسْعٌ وَّعِشْرُوْنَ سَاعَةً.
The Rule 4: remember that the tens themselves from 20 to 90 will remain the same regardless of the gender of the Tameez, e.g. ثَلَاثُوْنَ رَجُلًا and ثَلَاثُوْنَ امْرَأَةً.

Exercise 2 (أُكْتُبِ الْأَرْقَامَ بِالْحُرُوْفِ — write the figures out in words): eight figures from 21 to 30 with a feminine counted noun, ٢١ سَاعَةً، ٢٢ كُرَّاسَةً، ٢٥ زَهْرَةً، ٢٣ شَجَرَةً، ٢٦ طِفْلَةً، ٢٨ امْرَأَةً، ٢٤ تِلْمِيْذَةً، ٣٠ مُدَرِّسَةً.

sentences.en: These are a hundred and one books
and in the box there are a hundred and two books
and in the cupboard there are a hundred and three books
and in the storeroom there are a hundred and ten books

sentences.ar: فِي الْمَدْرَسَةِ مِائَةٌ وَّأَحَدَ عَشَرَ طَالِبًا
sentences.en: There are a hundred and eleven students in the school

sentences.en: and in the aeroplane there are a hundred and twelve passengers

sentences.ar: وَفِي الْقِطَارِ مِائَةٌ وَّثَلَاثَةَ عَشَرَ رَاكِبًا
sentences.en: and in the train there are a hundred and thirteen passengers

sentences.ar: وَفِي السَّفِيْنَةِ مِائَةٌ وَّخَمْسَةٌ وَّثَمَانُوْنَ رَاكِبًا

sentences.en: and at the harbour there are a hundred and ninety-one passengers

translateToEnglish.en: The Noble Qur'aan is thirty parts

translateToEnglish.ar: أَلشَّهْرُ ثَلَاثُوْنَ يَوْمًا أَوْ تِسْعَةٌ وَّعِشْرُوْنَ يَوْمًا
translateToEnglish.en: The month is thirty days or twenty-nine days
There are seventy-five students in the class
These are one hundred labourers

notesEn: The Rule 1: the Tameez of the number 100 is always singular and Majroor.
The Rule 2: if the number 100 is followed by another number, the Tameez will be according to the nature of that number, e.g. مِائَةٌ وَّعَشَرَةُ كُتُبٍ، مِائَةٌ وَّخَمْسَةٌ وَّأَرْبَعُوْنَ كِتَابًا.
