sentences.en: In the box there are a hundred and ninety-one clocks
In a rupee there are a hundred paisa

translateToEnglish.ar: فِي الْقُرْآنِ الْكَرِيْمِ مِائَةٌ وَّأَرْبَعَ عَشَرَةَ سُوْرَةً
translateToEnglish.en: In the Noble Qur'aan there are a hundred and fourteen chapters
In Soorah Al-Mulk there are thirty verses
In the class there are sixty-five female students
On the tree there are a hundred and eighty apples
In the pocket there are a hundred rupees

translateToEnglish.ar: عَلَى الْغُصْنِ مِائَةٌ وَّتِسْعٌ وَّتِسْعُوْنَ وَرَقَةً
translateToEnglish.en: On the branch there are a hundred and ninety-nine leaves

notesEn: The Rule 1: the Tameez of the number 100 is always singular and Majroor.

The Rule 2: if the number 100 is followed by another number, the Tameez will be according to the nature of that number, according to the rules of numbers up to 99, e.g. مِائَةٌ وَّعَشَرُ رَكَعَاتٍ، مِائَةٌ وَّخَمْسٌ وَّأَرْبَعُوْنَ كُرَّاسَةً.
The Rule 3: the Alif after the م in the word مِائَة is written but not read.
This lesson is the feminine counterpart of Lesson Sixty: the tens themselves are unchanged, but the Tameez is feminine, e.g. عَشَرُ كُرَّاسَاتٍ، عِشْرُوْنَ كُرَّاسَةً.

Exercise 2 (أُكْتُبِ الْأَرْقَامَ بِالْحُرُوْفِ — write the figures out in words): eight figures above one hundred with a feminine counted noun, ١١١ كُرَّاسَةً، ١١٣ سَاعَةً، ١٢٢ زَهْرَةً، ١٥٠ طِفْلَةً، ١٧١ امْرَأَةً، ١٨٥ تِلْمِيْذَةً، ١٩٣ سَيَّارَةً، ١٩٩ رُوْبِيَّةً.

lessons.topicEn: Counting in hundreds and the movement of numbers

sentences.en: In the ship there are a thousand passengers

sentences.ar: وَفِي الطَّائِرَةِ ثَلَاثُ مِائَةٍ وَّخَمْسُوْنَ رَاكِبًا
sentences.en: and in the aeroplane there are three hundred and fifty passengers
In the college there are nine hundred female students

sentences.ar: ثَمَنُ هٰذِهِ السَّيَّارَةِ ثَمَانُوْنَ أَلْفَ رُوْبِيَّةٍ
sentences.en: The price of this car is eighty thousand rupees

sentences.ar: أُجْرَةُ الطَّائِرَةِ مِنْ كَرَاتِشِيْ إِلَى إِسْلَام آبَاد أَلْفٌ وَّمِائَتَانِ وَخَمْسُوْنَ رُوْبِيَّةً
sentences.en: The aeroplane fare from Karachi to Islamabad is one thousand two hundred and fifty rupees
In the university there are three thousand students
The residents of this town are a million people

sentences.ar: فِي الْمَصْنَعِ أَلْفَانِ وَسِتُّ مِائَةِ عَامِلٍ
sentences.en: In the factory there are two thousand six hundred labourers

translateToEnglish.ar: اشْتَرَيْتُ الْكُتُبَ بِأَلْفٍ وَّخَمْسِ مِائَةِ رُوْبِيَّةٍ
translateToEnglish.en: I bought the books for one thousand five hundred rupees
Khaalid sold the house for a million rupees

translateToEnglish.ar: ثَمَنُ هٰذِهِ الْحَدِيْقَةِ ثَلَاثَةُ مَلَايِيْنَ رُوْبِيَّةٍ
translateToEnglish.en: The price of this garden is three million rupees

translateToEnglish.ar: فِي الْقِطَارِ أَلْفَانِ وَسَبْعُ مِائَةِ رَاكِبٍ
translateToEnglish.en: In the train there are two thousand seven hundred passengers

translateToEnglish.ar: مُرَتَّبُ هٰذَا الْخَادَمِ تِسْعُ مِائَةِ رُوْبِيَّةٍ
translateToEnglish.en: The salary of this servant is nine hundred rupees
In the school there are five thousand students

translateToEnglish.ar: فِي الْمَسْجِدِ اثْنَا عَشَرَ أَلْفَ مُصَلٍّ
translateToEnglish.en: In the mosque there are twelve thousand worshippers

notesEn: The Rule 1: the Tameez of the number 100, thousand and million is always singular and Majroor, and the same regardless of the gender.
The Rule 2: if these numbers are followed by another number, the Tameez will be according to the nature of that number.
The hundreds from 300 to 900 are formed with the feminine counting word before مِائَةٍ, e.g. ثَلَاثُ مِائَةٍ، ثَمَانُ مِائَةٍ, while the thousands take the masculine form, e.g. ثَلَاثَةُ آلَافٍ.

Book pages 172-173 print a full reference table headed جَدْوَلُ الْأَعْدَاد (Counting Table), listing the numbers 1 to 100 in words alongside their figures, then the hundreds, thousands and millions up to عَشَرَةُ مَلَايِيْنَ (10,000,000). The whole table is recorded here. Note that the units keep their tanween before the tens and the following وَ carries a shadda, e.g. وَاحِدٌ وَّعِشْرُوْنَ, while اِثْنَانِ ends in a noon and so takes a plain وَ, e.g. اِثْنَانِ وَعِشْرُوْنَ.

Exercise 2 (أُكْتُبِ الْأَرْقَامَ بِالْحُرُوْفِ — write the figures out in words): eight figures in the hundreds and thousands, ٥٠٠ مِيْلٍ، ٣٠٠٠ جُنْدِي، ٢٥٠ كِتَابًا، ٣٢٠ قَلَمًا، ٩٩ دَرَجَةً، ١٠٠٠٠٠ رُوْبِيَّةً، ١٨٥ نُسْخَةً، ٧٣٠ عَامِلًا.

sentences.ar: فِي الطَّائِرَةِ ثَلَاثُ مِائَةٍ وَّخَمْسُوْنَ رَاكِبًا
sentences.en: In the aeroplane there are three hundred and fifty passengers

sentences.ar: فِيْ قَاعَةِ الْإِنْتِظَارِ مِائَتَانِ وَثَمَانُوْنَ رَاكِبًا يَنْتَظِرُوْنَ الطَّائِرَةَ
sentences.en: In the waiting hall there are two hundred and eighty passengers waiting for the aeroplane

sentences.ar: دَخَلَ أَلْفَانِ وَتِسْعُ مِائَةِ طَالِبٍ فِي الْإِمْتِحَانِ
sentences.en: Two thousand nine hundred students entered the examination

sentences.ar: وَنَجَحَ مِنْهُمْ أَلْفَانِ وَثَمَانُ مِائَةٍ وَّتِسْعُوْنَ طَالِبًا
sentences.en: and two thousand eight hundred and ninety students among them were successful

sentences.ar: إِشْتَرَيْتُ الْكُتُبَ بِخَمْسَةِ آلَافٍ وَّسِتِّ مِائَةٍ وَّسَبْعٍ وَّعِشْرِيْنَ رُوْبِيَّةً
sentences.en: I bought the books for five thousand six hundred and twenty-seven rupees

sentences.ar: أَنْفَقْتُ فِيْ سَفَرِيْ خَمْسًا وَّعِشْرِيْنَ أَلْفًا وَّثَمَانَ مِائَةٍ وَّسِتًّا وَّعِشْرِيْنَ رُوْبِيَّةً
sentences.en: I spent twenty-five thousand eight hundred and twenty-six rupees on my journey

notesEn: This is a dictation lesson (أَلْإِمْلَاءُ): the Arabic page prints a word list and a short set of sentences to be dictated, and the English page prints the principles of writing the Hamzah Qat`i. There is no translation exercise.
Some Principles of Dictation, 1: if a Hamzah Qat`i appears inside a word, has a Dhamma on it, and is not followed by a letter of Madd (ا, و or ي), the Hamzah Qat`i will be written in the form of a و.

Some Principles of Dictation, 2: if the letter following the Hamzah Qat`i is a letter of Madd, one of the following will take place: if both the letters before and after the Hamzah Qat`i are joined to it, the Hamzah Qat`i will be written upon a curve; if the letters before and after the Hamzah Qat`i are not joined to it, the Hamzah Qat`i will be written as a separate Hamzah.
The dictation word list is printed under the heading أَلْمُفْرَدَاتُ with no English beside it; the English given here is supplied.

The word list is the point of the lesson: the first three words carry a separate Hamzah after a letter that does not join forwards (رَءُوْفٌ، يَقْرَءُوْنَ، رُءُوْسٌ), while the next two carry the Hamzah on a curve after a letter that does join forwards (مَسْئُوْلٌ، قَئُوْلٌ).

The book spells the same word two ways on facing pages: the word list on page 174 prints رَءُوْفٌ with a free-standing Hamzah, while the rule example on page 175 prints رُؤُوْفٌ with the Hamzah on a Waw. Both readings were confirmed at high magnification. The inline examples printed with the three rules are not reproduced above because the remaining Hamzah seats in them could not be read reliably.

sentences.en: The small hand is for the hour
and the big one is for the minute
and the smallest is for the second
There are twenty-four hours in a day
and sixty minutes in an hour
and sixty seconds in a minute
It is now a quarter past one
It is now half past one
It is now a quarter to two
It is now ten minutes past one

sentences.ar: السَّاعَةُ الْآنَ الثَّانِيَةُ إِلَّا خَمْسَ دَقَائِقَ
sentences.en: It is now five minutes to two

sentences.ar: تَبْدَأُ الْمَدْرَسَةُ السَّاعَةَ السَّابِعَةَ صَبَاحًا فِي الصَّيْفِ
sentences.en: The school starts at seven o'clock in the morning in summer
and it ends at eleven o'clock

sentences.ar: ثُمَّ تَبْدَأُ السَّاعَةَ الثَّالِثَةَ مَسَاءً وَتَنْتَهِي السَّاعَةَ الْخَامِسَةَ مَسَاءً
sentences.en: then it starts at three in the afternoon and ends at five in the evening

sentences.ar: أَمَّا فِي الشِّتَاءِ فَتَبْدَأُ الْمَدْرَسَةُ السَّاعَةَ الثَّامِنَةَ صَبَاحًا
sentences.en: As for winter, the school starts at eight o'clock in the morning
and it ends at twelve o'clock

sentences.ar: ثُمَّ تَبْدَأُ السَّاعَةَ الثَّانِيَةَ بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ وَتَنْتَهِي الرَّابِعَةَ مَسَاءً
sentences.en: then it starts at two in the afternoon and ends at four in the evening
It starts at two in the afternoon
It ends at four in the evening

qaPairs.answerAr: جِئْتُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ السَّاعَةَ السَّابِعَةَ وَالنِّصْفِ
أَعُوْدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ السَّاعَةَ الْحَادِيَةَ عَشَرَةَ وَالنِّصْفِ

qaPairs.questionAr: يَا فَاطِمَةُ! مَتٰى جِئْتِ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ؟
qaPairs.answerAr: جِئْتُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ السَّاعَةَ السَّابِعَةَ وَالنِّصْفِ
أَعُوْدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ السَّاعَةَ الثَّالِثَةَ بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ

translateToArabic.en: Khaalid! Do you have a watch?
When do you go to school?
I go to school at half past seven
translateToArabic.ar: أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ فِي السَّاعَةِ السَّابِعَةِ وَالنِّصْفِ

translateToArabic.en: When do you return from school?
I return at three in the afternoon
Until when do you study at night?
translateToArabic.ar: إِلٰى مَتٰى تَسْتَمِرُّ فِي الدُّرُوْسِ لَيْلًا؟

translateToArabic.en: I study until eleven at night
translateToArabic.ar: أَسْتَمِرُّ فِي الدُّرُوْسِ حَتَّى السَّاعَةِ الْحَادِيَةَ عَشَرَةَ لَيْلًا

translateToEnglish.ar: أَسْتَيْقِظُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ السَّاعَةَ الْخَامِسَةَ صَبَاحًا
translateToEnglish.en: I wake up every day at five o'clock in the morning
and I perform wudoo', pray and recite the Noble Qur'aan

translateToEnglish.ar: وَفِي السَّاعَةِ السَّادِسَةِ وَالنِّصْفِ أَتَنَاوَلُ الْفَطُوْرَ
translateToEnglish.en: and at half past six I have breakfast
and I read my books for a little while

translateToEnglish.ar: وَفِي السَّاعَةِ السَّابِعَةِ وَالنِّصْفِ أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ
translateToEnglish.en: and at half past seven I go to school

translateToEnglish.ar: وَأَسْتَمِرُّ فِي الدُّرُوْسِ حَتَّى السَّاعَةِ الْحَادِيَةَ عَشَرَةَ وَالنِّصْفِ
translateToEnglish.en: and I stay busy with the lessons until half past eleven

translateToEnglish.ar: ثُمَّ أَرْجِعُ إِلٰى بَيْتِيْ وَأَتَنَاوَلُ الْغَدَاءَ وَأَسْتَرِيْحُ قَلِيْلًا
translateToEnglish.en: then I return to my house, have lunch and rest a little

translateToEnglish.ar: وَفِي السَّاعَةِ الْوَاحِدَةِ وَالنِّصْفِ أُصَلِّي الظُّهْرَ
translateToEnglish.en: and at half past one I pray Zuhr

translateToEnglish.ar: وَفِي السَّاعَةِ الثَّانِيَةِ وَالنِّصْفِ أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ
translateToEnglish.en: and at half past two I go to school

translateToEnglish.ar: وَأَسْتَمِرُّ فِي الدُّرُوْسِ حَتَّى السَّاعَةِ الرَّابِعَةِ وَالنِّصْفِ
translateToEnglish.en: and I stay busy with the lessons until half past four
It is now three in the afternoon
It is now five o'clock
It is now ten o'clock in the morning
It is now one o'clock and forty minutes
It is now twelve o'clock

translateToEnglish.ar: السَّاعَةُ الْآنَ الرَّابِعَةُ إِلَّا خَمْسَ دَقَائِقَ
translateToEnglish.en: It is now five minutes to four

notesEn: Telling the time: the hour is named with the feminine ordinal after السَّاعَةُ, e.g. السَّاعَةُ الْآنَ الْوَاحِدَةُ. Add وَالرُّبْعُ for a quarter past, وَالنِّصْفُ for half past, and وَعَشَرُ دَقَائِقَ for minutes past; use إِلَّا for minutes to the hour, e.g. الثَّانِيَةُ إِلَّا رُبْعًا، الرَّابِعَةُ إِلَّا خَمْسَ دَقَائِقَ.
The parts of the day are given as صَبَاحًا (in the morning), بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ (in the afternoon) and مَسَاءً (in the evening).

Book page 176 prints the six time answers as question-and-answer pairs, each headed by the same question كَمِ السَّاعَةُ الْآنَ؟ beside a drawing of a clock face showing the time. Because the clock face cannot be reproduced here, those six answers are recorded as model sentences rather than as question-and-answer pairs, so that one question is not left with six different correct answers.

For the same reason, three of the twelve printed question-and-answer pairs on book page 177 repeat an earlier question word for word (مَتٰى تَنْتَهِي؟ twice more and وَمَتٰى تَبْدَأُ بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ؟ once more); their answers are kept as model sentences: تَنْتَهِي الثَّانِيَةَ عَشَرَةَ، تَبْدَأُ الثَّانِيَةَ بَعْدَ الظُّهْرِ، تَنْتَهِي الرَّابِعَةَ مَسَاءً.

Exercise 4 (أَجِبْ عَنِ الْأَسْئِلَةِ التَّالِيَةِ — answer the following questions) prints nine questions. The first, كَمِ السَّاعَةُ الْآنَ؟, has no determinate answer and is left out; the other eight are answered here from the lesson's own sentences.

sentences.en: There are seven days in a week

sentences.ar: وَهِيَ: السَّبْتُ، وَالْأَحَدُ، وَالْإِثْنَيْنِ، وَالثُّلَاثَاءُ، وَالْأَرْبِعَاءُ، وَالْخَمِيْسُ، وَالْجُمْعَةُ
sentences.en: and they are: Saturday, Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday

sentences.ar: نَحْنُ فِيْ يَوْمِ السَّبْتِ وَغَدًا يَوْمُ الْأَحَدِ
sentences.en: We are on Saturday and tomorrow is Sunday
and the day after tomorrow is Monday
and the day before yesterday was Thursday
Friday is the best of days
and it is a blessed day
Friday is a holiday at the school

sentences.ar: لَا نَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ يَوْمَ الْجُمْعَةِ
sentences.en: We do not go to the school on Friday

sentences.ar: بَلْ نَغْتَسِلُ وَنَلْبَسُ ثِيَابًا جَدِيْدَةً أَوْ مَغْسُوْلَةً
sentences.en: rather we bathe and wear new or washed clothes

sentences.ar: ثُمَّ نَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَسْجِدِ الْجَامِعِ وَنُصَلِّي الْجُمْعَةَ
sentences.en: then we go to the Jaami' Masjid and pray the Jumu'ah

qaPairs.questionAr: هَلْ تَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ يَوْمَ الْجُمْعَةِ؟
qaPairs.answerAr: لَا أَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ يَوْمَ الْجُمْعَةِ

translateToArabic.en: Classes take place 6 days a week
Arabic Madrassahs have their holiday on Fridays and continue classes on Sundays
translateToArabic.ar: أَلْمَدَارِسُ الْعَرَبِيَّةُ عُطْلَتُهَا يَوْمَ الْجُمْعَةِ وَالدِّرَاسَةُ فِيْهَا يَوْمَ الْأَحَدِ

translateToArabic.en: My brother will reach Karachi on Thursday
translateToArabic.ar: يَصِلُ أَخِيْ إِلٰى كَرَاتشِيْ يَوْمَ الْخَمِيْسِ

translateToArabic.en: I will leave for Lahore on Monday
Mail does not arrive on Fridays
The Haaji's plane will arrive on Wednesday

translateToEnglish.en: Allah made the day for work
and He made the night for rest

translateToEnglish.ar: يُوْجَدُ عِبَادٌ صَالِحُوْنَ يُصَلُّوْنَ بِاللَّيْلِ وَيَصُوْمُوْنَ بِالنَّهَارِ
translateToEnglish.en: There are righteous servants who pray by night and fast by day
The labourers work by night and by day
and in summer and winter, and in heat and cold
The train runs by night and by day

translateToEnglish.ar: وَيَنْقُلُ الرُّكَّابَ مِنْ بَلَدٍ إِلٰى بَلَدٍ
translateToEnglish.en: and it carries the passengers from one town to another

notesEn: The days of the week are named with the definite article: السَّبْتُ، الْأَحَدُ، الْإِثْنَيْنِ، الثُّلَاثَاءُ، الْأَرْبِعَاءُ، الْخَمِيْسُ، الْجُمْعَةُ. The week begins with الْأَحَد (Sunday), and يَوْمُ الْجُمْعَةِ is described as أَفْضَلُ الْأَيَّامِ (the best of days).

To say what day it is, use يَوْمُ with the day name, e.g. غَدًا يَوْمُ الْأَحَدِ (tomorrow is Sunday), بَعْدَ غَدٍ يَوْمُ الْإِثْنَيْنِ (the day after tomorrow is Monday), أَمْسِ كَانَ يَوْمُ الْجُمْعَةِ (yesterday was Friday), قَبْلَ الْأَمْسِ (the day before yesterday). For an action on a given day the day is Mansoob, e.g. يَوْمَ الْجُمْعَةِ.
The مَعَانِي الْكَلِمَات table runs across two book pages: the days of the week and أُسْبُوْع on page 181, then ten more words on page 182, which is where the lesson ends.
The printed question-and-answer pairs give أَمْسِ as Sunday while the reading passage gives it as Friday; both are recorded as printed.

sentences.en: There are twelve months in a year
The Muslims fast in the blessed Ramadaan
and it is the best of months
and in it the Noble Qur'aan was revealed

sentences.ar: تَبْدَأُ الدِّرَاسَةُ فِي الْمَدْرَسَةِ فِيْ شَوَّالٍ
sentences.en: Classes at the school begin in Shawwaal
and the annual holiday at the school is two months

sentences.ar: تَبْدَأُ مِنْ نِصْفِ شَعْبَانَ وَتَنْتَهِيْ إِلٰى مُنْتَصَفِ شَوَّالٍ
sentences.en: It begins from the middle of Sha'baan and ends at the middle of Shawwaal

qaPairs.answerAr: نَزَلَ الْقُرْآنُ الْكَرِيْمُ فِيْ رَمَضَانَ الْمُبَارَكِ

translateToEnglish.en: In the blessed Ramadaan mercy descends

translateToEnglish.ar: يَبْدَأُ اخْتِبَارُ الْفَتْرَةِ الْأُوْلٰى فِيْ صَفَرٍ
translateToEnglish.en: The first term examination begins in Safar
and the annual examination begins in Sha'baan
My father travels for Hajj in Shawwaal

notesEn: The lunar year has twelve months: مُحَرَّمٌ، صَفَرٌ، رَبِيْعُ الْأَوَّلِ، رَبِيْعُ الثَّانِيْ، جُمَادَى الْأُوْلٰى، جُمَادَى الثَّانِيَةِ، رَجَبٌ، شَعْبَانُ، رَمَضَانُ، شَوَّالٌ، ذُوالْقَعْدَةِ، ذُو الْحَجَّةِ. The reading passage prints them as a single list; they are recorded here one to an entry.
رَمَضَانُ is described as أَفْضَلُ الشُّهُوْرِ (the best of months), the month in which the Muslims fast and in which the Qur'aan was revealed; the Hajj is performed in ذِي الْحَجَّةِ.

The school year runs from شَوَّال to شَعْبَان, and the annual holiday is two months, from the middle of شَعْبَان to the middle of شَوَّال. Note مِنْ نِصْفِ and إِلٰى مُنْتَصَفِ for the middle of a month.
Exercise 2 (أُذْكُرِ الشُّهُوْرَ الْقَمَرِيَّةَ بِالتَّرْتِيْبِ — mention the lunar months in order) is answered by the twelve lunar months above.

Book page 184 also prints a table headed أَلشُّهُوْرُ الشَّمْسِيَّةُ الْعَرَبِيَّةُ وَالْإِنْجِلِيْزِيَّةُ, giving each solar month twice: the Arabic name, recorded here, and underneath it the English name in Arabic letters, which is printed without harakat and is not recorded: يناير، فبراير، مارس، ابريل، مايو، يونيو، يوليو، أغسطس، ستمبر، أكتوبر، نوفمبر، ديسمبر.

sentences.ar: بَدَأَ الْاِمْتِحَانُ السَّنَوِيُّ مِنْ أَوَّلِ شَعْبَانَ
sentences.en: The annual examination began from the first of Sha'baan
and it continued for six days
The students read their lessons, understood them and memorised them
and they answered the questions with good answers

sentences.ar: وَخَرَجُوا مِنْ قَاعَةِ الْاِمْتِحَانِ فَرِحِيْنَ مَسْرُوْرِيْنَ
sentences.en: and they came out of the examination hall happy and delighted

sentences.ar: تَبْدَأُ الْإِجَازَةُ السَّنَوِيَّةُ مِنْ مُنْتَصِفِ شَعْبَانَ
sentences.en: The annual holiday begins from the middle of Sha'baan

sentences.ar: فَيَرْجِعُ الطُّلَّابُ إِلَى بِلَادِهِمْ لِزِيَارَةِ آبَائِهِمْ وَأُمَّهَاتِهِمْ وَأَقَارِبِهِمْ
sentences.en: so the students return to their home towns to visit their fathers, their mothers and their relatives

notesEn: Some Principles of Dictation. 1. If the Hamzah Qat`i appears at the end of a word, one of the following will take place:
If the letter before the Hamzah Qat`i has a Harkat, the Hamzah Qat`i will be written in the form that resembles the Harkat of the letter, e.g. قَرَأَ، أَنْبَأَ، قُرِئَ، أُنْبِئَ، وَضُؤَ.
If the letter before the Hamzah Qat`i has a Sukoon, the Hamzah Qat`i will be written as a separate Hamzah, e.g. دِفْءٌ، بُطْءٌ، مِلْءٌ، سَمَاءٌ، أَضَاءَ، شَيْءٌ، فَيْءٌ.

The Arabic page is a dictation drill. It opens with a word list headed أَلْمُفْرَدَات: قَرَأَ، أَنْبَأَ، قُرِئَ، وَضُؤَ، دِفْءٌ، بُطْءٌ، مِلْءٌ، سَمَاءٌ، أَضَاءَ، شَيْءٌ، فَيْءٌ، أَيَّامٌ، إِجَازَةٌ، الْمَسْجِدُ الْجَامِعُ، ذُو الْقَعْدَة، ذُو الْحِجَّة — and is followed by the two short passages headed أَلْجُمَل that are listed under sentences.

sentences.en: He has one brother and one sister
Khaalid's brother, his name is Mahmood
and his sister, her name is Faatimah
and Mahmood's age is seven years
and Faatimah's age is five years
Khaalid's father, his name is Haamid
and his mother, her name is Zaynab
Haamid has three brothers and two sisters
and Zaynab has two brothers and four sisters
Haamid's brothers are Khaalid's paternal uncles
and his sisters are Khaalid's paternal aunts
Zaynab's brothers are Khaalid's maternal uncles
and her sisters are Khaalid's maternal aunts
Haamid's father, his name is Sa'eed
and his mother, her name is Sa'eedah
and it is kind to people

translateToArabic.en: Zaynab is Haamid's wife and he is her husband
What work does your father do?
Mahmood was born on a Friday

translateToEnglish.en: The righteous boy obeys his Lord
and he is good to his parents
and he loves his brothers and his sisters
he honours their elders and is merciful to their little ones

translateToEnglish.ar: وَيَحْتَرِمُ أَعْمَامَهُ وَأَخْوَالَهُ وَعَمَّاتِهِ وَأَخَوَاتِهِ وَأَقَارِبَهُ
translateToEnglish.en: and he respects his paternal uncles, his maternal uncles, his paternal aunts, his sisters and his relatives
and he visits them and is good to them
and he loves his teacher and his classmates and visits them
and he plays with his classmates politely
and he does not harm any one of them

translateToEnglish.ar: وَلَا يَضْرِبُ الصِّغَارَ وَلَا يُؤْذِي الْجَارَ
translateToEnglish.en: and he does not hit the little ones nor harm the neighbour

notesEn: Book page 187 opens with a family tree of Khaalid drawn above the passage: سَعِيْد (labelled جَدُّ خَالِدٍ) at the top; below him his children, read right to left, نَعِيْمَة، جَمِيْلَة، حَامِد، نَعِيْم، سَلِيْم، نَسِيْم, with the two girls bracketed عَمَّات خَالِد and the three boys bracketed أَعْمَام خَالِد; and a bottom row فَاطِمَة (أُخْت) – خَالِد – مَحْمُوْد (أَخُوْ).

sentences.en: Khaalid is a pupil in the school

sentences.ar: هُوَ لَا يَذْهَبُ الْيَوْمَ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ؛ لِأَنَّهُ مَرِيْضٌ
sentences.en: He is not going to school today, because he is ill

sentences.ar: فَيَكْتُبُ طَلَبًا وَيُرْسِلُهُ إِلَى مُدِيْرِ التَّعْلِيْمِ
sentences.en: so he writes a request and sends it to the principal

sentences.ar: السَّيِّدُ مُدِيْرُ التَّعْلِيْمِ بِجَامِعَةِ الْعُلُوْمِ الْإِسْلَامِيَّةِ، حَفِظَهُ اللهُ تَعَالَى
sentences.en: The respected principal of Jaami'atul Uloomil Islaamiyyah — may Allaah Most High protect him
Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allaah and His blessings

sentences.ar: لَقَدْ أَصَابَنِيْ أَلَمٌ شَدِيْدٌ فِيْ رَأْسِيْ
sentences.en: A severe pain has struck me in my head

sentences.ar: وَلَا أَسْتَطِيْعُ مَعَ الْمَرَضِ الْحُضُوْرَ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ
sentences.en: and with the illness I am unable to attend school
so please be so kind as to grant me two days' leave

sentences.ar: وَسَوْفَ أُطَالِعُ الدُّرُوْسَ الَّتِيْ تَفُوْتُنِيْ أَيَّامَ مَرَضِيْ
sentences.en: and I shall study the lessons that I miss during the days of my illness
and please accept my utmost thanks
the student of the first class

qaPairs.questionAr: لِمَاذَا لَمْ يَحْضُرْ مَحْمُوْدٌ فِي الْجَامِعَةِ؟

notesEn: The Rule: 1. When writing a request for permission, it is necessary to state the position of the addressee, e.g. السَّيِّدُ مُدِيْرُ التَّعْلِيْمِ or السَّيِّدُ مُدِيْرُ الْمَدْرَسَةِ.
The Rule: 2. Thereafter, state المحترم or a du'aa such as حَفِظَهُ اللهُ تَعَالَى.
The Rule: 3. Then state your request as briefly as possible.
The Rule: 4. If the addressee is a man of learning, address him with the words فَضِيْلَةُ الشَّيْخِ etc.

Exercise 1 is a composition task, not a translation drill: أُكْتُبْ طَلَبًا إِلَى الْمُدِيْرِ، وَاطْلُبْ فِيْهِ إِجَازَةَ يَوْمٍ؛ لِأَنَّكَ تَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَطَارِ لِاسْتِقْبَالِ الْحُجَّاجِ — write a request to the principal asking for one day's leave because you are going to the airport to receive the Hajj pilgrims.

sentences.en: My honourable father — may Allaah Most High protect you

sentences.ar: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَةُ اللهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ، وَبَعْدُ:
sentences.en: Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allaah and His blessings. To proceed:

sentences.ar: فَقَدْ وَصَلْتُ إِلَى كَرَاتْشِيْ فِيْ عَشَرِ شَوَّالٍ
sentences.en: I reached Karachi on the tenth of Shawwaal
and I joined Jaami'atul Uloomil Islaamiyyah
and I was accepted into the first class
and I started learning the Arabic language

sentences.ar: وَالْآنَ بَعْدَ زَمَنٍ قَلِيْلٍ أَتَكَلَّمُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ وَأَفْهَمُهَا
sentences.en: and now, after a short time, I speak Arabic and understand it
and I know how to read and write it, all praise belongs to Allaah

sentences.ar: وَإِنِّيْ لَفَرِحٌ أَنْ أَكْتُبَ إِلَيْكُمْ هٰذَا الْخِطَابَ بِاللُّغَةِ الْعَرَبِيَّةِ
sentences.en: And I am truly delighted to write this letter to you in the Arabic language

sentences.ar: وَأَرْجُوْ أَنْ أَعُوْدَ إِلَيْكُمْ فِيْ آخِرِ هٰذَا الْعَامِ
sentences.en: and I hope to return to you at the end of this year

sentences.ar: وَقَدْ تَعَلَّمْتُ كَثِيْرًا مِنَ اللُّغَةِ الْعَرَبِيَّةِ وَالْعُلُوْمِ الْإِسْلَامِيَّةِ إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ
sentences.en: having learnt much of the Arabic language and the Islaamic sciences, if Allaah wills

sentences.ar: وَتَحِيَّاتِيْ إِلَى الْوَالِدَةِ الْمُحْتَرَمَةِ، وَإِخْوَانِيْ وَأَخَوَاتِيْ وَجَمِيْعِ أَصْدِقَائِيْ
sentences.en: And my greetings to my respected mother, my brothers, my sisters and all my friends

notesEn: The Rule: 1. The purpose of a letter it to inform the addressee about one's circumstances and whatever is on one's mind. For this reason, it is necessary to use clear and simple language. Avoid elaborate speech.
The Rule: 2. Titles should therefore also be brief. Use words like الكريم and المحترم when addressing seniors and words like العزيز and الحبيب when addressing juniors.
The Rule: 3. Also remember to write: اَلسَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ وَرَحْمَةُ اللهِ وَبَرَكَاتُهُ

Exercise 1 is a composition task, not a translation drill: أُكْتُبْ رِسَالَةً إِلَى أَخِيْكَ، وَأَخْبِرْهُ أَنَّكَ نَجَحْتَ فِي الْامْتِحَانِ السَّنَوِيِّ — write a letter to your brother telling him that you passed the annual examination.
The letter is headed by the place name كَرَاتْشِيْ above the salutation, and closes with وَالسَّلَام, the signature ابْنُكُمْ: خَالِد and a blank التَّارِيخ (date) line.

sentences.ar: تَدْرُسُ فِيْ مَدْرَسَةِ الْبَنَاتِ وَتَتَعَلَّمُ اللُّغَةَ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ
sentences.en: She studies in the girls' school and learns the Arabic language
and her brother works in Lahore
so she wrote the following letter to her brother

sentences.ar: الْأَخُ الْكَرِيْمُ عَبْدُ الْحَمِيْد – حَفِظَكُمُ اللهُ تَعَالَى
sentences.en: My honourable brother Abdul Hameed — may Allaah Most High protect you
Peace be upon you, and the mercy of Allaah and His blessings

sentences.ar: أَرْجُوْ أَنْ تَكُوْنَ بِأَحْسَنِ حَالٍ وَأَتَمِّ صِحَّةٍ وَعَافِيَةٍ
sentences.en: I hope that you are in the best of states and in complete health and well-being

sentences.ar: وَلَعَلَّهُ يَسُرُّكَ أَنِّيْ دَخَلْتُ فِيْ مَدْرَسَةِ الْبَنَاتِ هٰذَا الْعَامَ
sentences.en: and it may please you that I have entered the girls' school this year

sentences.ar: وَبَدَأْتُ أَتَعَلَّمُ الْقُرْآنَ الْكَرِيْمَ، وَاللُّغَةَ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ، وَالْعُلُوْمَ الْمُفِيْدَةَ
sentences.en: and have started learning the Noble Qur'aan, the Arabic language and the beneficial sciences

sentences.ar: وَأَرْجُوْ أَنْ تَعُوْدَ فِيْ آخِرِ هٰذَا الْعَامِ فِي الْإِجَازَةِ
sentences.en: And I hope that you will return at the end of this year during the holidays

sentences.ar: وَتَجِدُنِيْ أَتَكَلَّمُ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ وَأَفْهَمُهَا جَيِّدًا إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ تَعَالَى
sentences.en: and find me speaking Arabic and understanding it well, if Allaah Most High wills

sentences.ar: وَإِنِّيْ أَذْهَبُ دَائِمًا إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ مُبَكِّرَةً
sentences.en: And I always go to school early
and I respect my teacher and work hard at my lessons

sentences.ar: وَعِنْدَ مَا أَعُوْدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ أَلْعَبُ مَعَ الْأَخِ الصَّغِيْرِ سَعِيْد قَلِيْلًا
sentences.en: and when I return home I play a little with my little brother Sa'eed

sentences.ar: وَالْوَالِدُ وَالْوَالِدَةُ وَالْإِخْوَةُ وَالْأَخَوَاتُ كُلُّهُمْ بِخَيْرٍ
sentences.en: Father, mother, the brothers and the sisters are all well
and they send you their greetings and pray for you

notesEn: Exercise 1 is a sequencing drill, not a translation drill: Abdul Hameed's reply to Faatimah is printed as twelve numbered fragments that are out of order, and the student must arrange them in the correct sequence.
The letter is headed by the place name مُلْتَان above the salutation and closes with وَالسَّلَام, the signature أُخْتُكَ: فَاطِمَةُ and a blank التَّارِيخ (date) line.

sentences.en: He does not utter an indecent word

sentences.ar: وَلَا يُؤْذِيْ أَحَدًا فِي الْبَيْتِ أَوِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ
sentences.en: and he does not hurt anyone at home or at school

sentences.ar: وَإِذَا دَخَلَ الْمَنْزِلَ وَوَجَدَ ضُيُوْفًا سَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَصَافَحَهُمْ
sentences.en: and when he enters the house and finds guests he greets them and shakes their hands

sentences.ar: وَلَا يَجْلِسُ مَعَهُمْ إِلَّا إِذَا أَمَرَهُ أَبُوْهُ بِالْجُلُوْسِ
sentences.en: and he does not sit with them unless his father tells him to sit

sentences.ar: وَإِذَا طَلَبَ شَيْئًا مِنْ وَالِدِهِ أَوْ أُمِّهِ تَكَلَّمَ بِأَدَبٍ وَاحْتِرَامٍ
sentences.en: and when he asks his father or his mother for something he speaks with politeness and respect

sentences.ar: وَإِذَا أَخَذَ شَيْئًا مِنْ أَحَدٍ قَالَ لَهُ: جَزَاكَ اللهُ خَيْرًا
sentences.en: and when he takes something from someone he says to him: may Allaah reward you well
And he is clean in clothing and body
and his belongings are tidy and clean
for that reason his father and his brothers love him
just as everyone who knows him loves him

sentences.ar: وَيَقُوْلُ النَّاسُ عَنْهُ: إِنَّهُ تِلْمِيْذٌ مُؤَدَّب
sentences.en: and people say about him: he is a well-mannered pupil

notesEn: Exercise 1 is a rewriting drill, not a translation drill: اجْعَلْ بَدَلَ خَالِدٍ فِي الدَّرْسِ الْمَاضِيْ زَيْنَبَ — retell the passage with Zaynab in place of Khaalid, beginning زَيْنَبُ تِلْمِيْذَةٌ مُؤَدَّبَةٌ، لَا تَنْطِقُ بِكَلِمَةٍ بَذِيْئَةٍ، وَلَا تُؤْذِيْ أَحَدًا فِي الْبَيْتِ أَوِ الْمَدْرَسَةِ ... إلخ
Note the Following: When changing a passage, remember to change the gender of the Dhameers also when you change the gender of the verbs, e.g. أَمَرَهُ أَبُوْهُ will change to أَمَرَهَا أَبُوْهَا.
Note the Following: When changing from male to female, also remember to change some words to suitable alternatives, e.g. one would change ضُيُوْف to ضِيْفَاتِ.
Note the Following: مَثَلًا إِذَا دَخَلَتِ الْمَنْزِلَ وَوَجَدَتِ الضَّيْفَاتِ سَلَّمَتْ عَلَيْهِنَّ.

sentences.ar: كَانَ أَمِيْرُ الْمُؤْمِنِيْنَ عُمَرُ بنُ الْخَطَّابِ -رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ- سَائِرًا فِي الطَّرِيْقِ ذَاتَ يَوْمٍ
sentences.en: One day the Commander of the Believers, 'Umar ibn al-Khattaab - may Allah be pleased with him - was walking along the road
and he saw children playing here and there

sentences.ar: فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ مُقْبِلًا عَلَيْهِمْ هَرَبُوْا إِلَّا صَبِيًّا مِنْهُمْ
sentences.en: and when they saw him coming towards them they fled, except one boy among them

sentences.ar: بَقِيَ مَكَانَهُ حَتَّى جَاءَهُ عُمَرُ -رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ- فَقَالَ لَهُ
sentences.en: He remained in his place until 'Umar - may Allah be pleased with him - came to him and said to him
What is your name, O boy?
So he answered him: My name is 'Abdullaah

sentences.ar: فَقَالَ لَهُ عُمَرُ -رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ-: لِمَ لَمْ تَهْرُب مَعَ أَصْحَابِكَ؟
sentences.en: Then 'Umar - may Allah be pleased with him - said to him: Why did you not run away with your companions?

sentences.ar: فَأَجَابَ الصَّبِيُّ فِي شَجَاعَةٍ: يَا أَمِيْرَ الْمُؤْمِنِيْنَ!
sentences.en: So the boy answered bravely: O Commander of the Believers!
I have not committed a sin that I should fear you
and the road is not narrow that I should widen it for you

sentences.ar: فَسَرَّ عُمَرُ -رَضِيَ اللهُ عَنْهُ- مِنْ شَجَاعَةِ الْغُلَامِ وَذَكَائِهِ وَحُسْنِ جَوَابِهِ
sentences.en: So 'Umar - may Allah be pleased with him - was delighted at the boy's bravery, his intelligence and the excellence of his reply

qaPairs.questionAr: هَلْ هَرَبَ عَبْدُ اللهِ مَعَ أَصْحَابِهِ؟
qaPairs.answerAr: لَمْ يَهْرُبْ عَبْدُ اللهِ مَعَ أَصْحَابِهِ

translateToEnglish.en: A teacher went out for a stroll
and he saw his pupils playing in the field
he saw them playing politely

translateToEnglish.ar: لَا يُخَاصِمُوْنَ وَلَا يَشْتِمُوْنَ وَلَا يَصْخَبُوْنَ بَلْ يَحْتَرِمُ بَعْضُهُمْ بَعْضًا
translateToEnglish.en: they do not quarrel, nor swear, nor make a noise; rather they respect one another
so he was pleased with them
and when they saw their teacher they left off playing
and they came to him and greeted him
so he returned the greeting to them and prayed for them

notesEn: Exercise 1 (تَرْجِمْ بِالإِنْجِلِيْزِيَّةِ) is a single running passage about a teacher and his well-behaved pupils; it has been split clause by clause in translateToEnglish.

Exercise 2 is a form-change drill, not a translation: غَيِّرِ الْأَفْعَالَ الْآتِيَةَ إِلَى الْأَفْعَالِ الْمُؤَنَّثَةِ - change the following verbs into the feminine: خَرَجَ، رَأَى، فَرِحَ، سَلَّمَ، دَعَا، يُخَاصِمُ، يَرُدُّ، يَشْتِمُ، يَصْخَبُ، يَحْتَرِمُ.

sentences.en: Say: I believe in Allah, then be steadfast
Say something good, otherwise remain silent
The best speech is that which is brief and to the point
The best of people are the most beneficial of them to people
The bane of knowledge is forgetfulness
The one who points towards good is like the one who does it
Every act of kindness is a charity
A good word is a charity
Asking questions is half of knowledge
A book is the best companion

translateToEnglish.en: Khaalid is a righteous boy
He does not talk much
He loves silence
and he loves cleanliness
He benefits his classmates
and he points them towards good
and he enjoins good upon them and forbids them from evil

notesEn: Exercise 1 (تَرْجِمْ بِالإِنْجِلِيْزِيَّةِ) is one running passage about a boy named Khaalid; it has been split clause by clause in translateToEnglish.
Exercise 2 is not a translation drill: اِحْفِظْ هٰذِهِ الْحِكَمَ وَالنَّصَائِحَ وَاسْتَعْمِلْهَا بَيْنَ الطُّلَّابِ - memorise these maxims and pieces of advice and use them among the students.

sentences.en: so the students head for the school
and they enter it in groups
and they gather in the school yard

sentences.ar: وَقَبْلَ أَنْ يَدْخُلُوْا فُصُوْلَهُمْ يَقِفُوْنَ فِيْهَا صُفُوْفًا
sentences.en: and before they enter their classrooms they stand there in rows
and they call upon Allah with this supplication

sentences.ar: يَا إِلٰهَ الْعَالَمِيْنَا يَا مُجِيْبَ السَّائِلِيْنَا
sentences.en: O God of the worlds, O Answerer of those who ask

sentences.ar: هَبْ لَنَا مِنْكَ رَشَادًا وَسَدَادًا وَيَقِيْنَا
sentences.en: Grant us from You right guidance, uprightness and certainty

sentences.ar: رَبِّ جَمِّلْنَا بِعِلْمٍ وَاهْدِنَا دُنْيَا وَدِيْنَا
sentences.en: My Lord, adorn us with knowledge and guide us in this world and in religion

sentences.ar: وَاحْمِنَا مِنْ كُلِّ سُوْءٍ وَانْشُرِ الْخَيْرَاتِ فِيْنَا
sentences.en: and protect us from every evil, and spread good things among us

sentences.ar: وَبَعْدَ مَا يَنْتَهُوْنَ مِنَ الدُّعَاءِ يَتَوَجَّهُوْنَ إِلَى فُصُوْلِ الدِّرَاسَةِ
sentences.en: And after they finish the supplication they head for the study classrooms
and they sit in their places
and they listen to the teacher

translateToEnglish.en: Supplication is the marrow of worship
Allah, the Exalted, said: “Call upon Me; I will answer you”

translateToEnglish.ar: وَقَالَ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَ إِذَا سَأَلَكَ عِبَادِيْ عَنِّيْ فَإِنِّيْ قَرِيْبٌ أُجِيْبُ دَعْوَةَ الدَّاعِ إِذَا دَعَانِ﴾
translateToEnglish.en: And He, the Exalted, said: “And when My servants ask you about Me, indeed I am near; I answer the call of the caller when he calls upon Me”

translateToEnglish.ar: وَقَالَ رَسُوْلُ اللهِ صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ: "إِذَا سَأَلْتَ فَاسْئَلِ اللهَ"
translateToEnglish.en: And the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: “When you ask, ask Allah”

notesEn: Exercise 1 (تَرْجِمْ بِالْإِنْجِلِيْزِيَّةِ - translate into English) is one running passage on du'aa' quoting two Qur'anic verses and a hadith; it has been split clause by clause in translateToEnglish.

NOTE printed after the exercise: the words أَلْعَالَمِيْنَا and أَلسَّائِلِيْنَا have been written with the letter (ا) at the end only to tie in with the poem; the words really are أَلْعَالَمِيْنَ and أَلسَّائِلِيْنَ.
The du'aa' itself is printed as a five-row table of verses; each row is one verse whose two hemistichs sit in the right and left cells, and it has been joined into a single line per verse.
